543066|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% YoY to INR609 crore on lower credit cost (7.7%), though FY27 cost-to-income guided at 55-58%.
543066|2026-03.overview: SBI Cards reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR5,187 crore (+7% YoY) and PAT of INR609 crore (+14% YoY), helped by gross credit cost falling 55 bps QoQ to 7.7% and GNPA down 46 bps QoQ to 2.41%. Receivables grew only about 2% YoY to INR56,926 crore, and management declined to guide on asset growth, tying it to card acquisition. FY26 PAT was INR2,167 crore (+13% YoY), with cost-to-income at 55.3% for the year after higher corporate-spend passback costs. Management expects revolver rates to drift down and is leaning on instalment lending to offset.

financial_highlights.change: management overlay retained at INR220 crore

segments.name: Card acquisition
segments.commentary: 917,000 new accounts added in Q4 against a 0.9-1.0 million quarterly target; FY26 sourcing mix 54% open market and 46% banca. Management said next quarter is expected in a similar range.

segments.name: Spends
segments.commentary: Q4 total spends above INR1.15 trillion (+31% YoY); retail spends INR89,786 crore (+13% YoY). FY26 total spends INR4.3 trillion, retail INR3.54 trillion (+15%). Online share of retail spends 62.5% in FY26; spend market share 18.1%.

segments.name: Receivables and revolve
segments.commentary: Receivables INR56,926 crore (~+2% YoY). Interest-earning assets 54%, revolver balance 22%; revolve rate has been 22-24% over two years with a slight downward bias expected in FY27.

segments.name: Other income
segments.commentary: Q4 other income elevated by one-offs: provision release and a tax-matter provision added in FY26; GST included in other income, PIDF reduction booked in expenses.

guidance_outlook: Cost-to-income expected in the 55-58% range for FY27, with no major step-up from corporate spends.
NIM expected to remain stable, at risk from any significant rise in cost of funds.
Credit cost expected to moderate further in FY27, dependent on geopolitical and macro developments.
No guidance on asset (receivables) growth; asset growth expected to follow card acquisition.
Medium-term ROA target of 4% to 4.5%, described as achievable.
No cost-of-funds guidance for FY27; around 70-75% of borrowings are floating (T-bill or repo linked) and reprice in 60-90 day buckets.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capacity figures, utilisation data or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the call covered only card acquisition volumes (917,000 new accounts in Q4 vs 0.9-1.0 million quarterly target, expected to be in a similar range next quarter) and asset growth tied to acquisition, with no asset growth guidance given.
Digital onboarding via SBI Card Sprint is described as growing in share of new account acquisitions; no capacity or cost figures were disclosed for it.
Management said it is poised to harness AI and ML investments in FY27 for product development, service delivery and collections; no capex amount or timeline was given.
Collections infrastructure, digital and physical, was strengthened during the year; no capex or capacity quantification was provided.
demand_pricing: Industry credit card spends grew ~12% YoY to INR23.62 trillion in FY26 per RBI; cards-in-force above 118.6 million; SBI Card cards-in-force share 18.6%.
Management attributed muted industry card growth to issuers tightening underwriting after asset quality issues, with few new-to-credit customers being acquired.
Banca NTC/NTCC share estimated at 20-30% of banca-sourced customers; Q4 new-sourcing mix 70% salaried.
Rental spends are now a very small category after fee levy; UPI-on-credit growth 10% in Q4 vs Q3.
Management said FY26 corporate spends (with passback costs) raised both income and opex, thinning margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is new account addition lower, and what is the cost-to-income outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 acquisition of 917,000 was on track with the 0.9-1.0 million target; cost-to-income guided 55-58% for FY27 as corporate-spend passback costs normalise, not employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revolver downside plan and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a revolver floor; first offset is instalment lending rather than cutting rewards. Cost of funds guidance deferred given RBI and geopolitical uncertainty; repricing to continue for about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-quarter INR100 crore management overlay increase run through P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR100 crore additional ECL provision is charged to P&L; without it profit would be INR100 crore higher. Overlay retained at INR220 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the dividend paid when profit growth was ~13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capital adequacy (25.5%) is comfortable and the company is underleveraged, so INR2.50 per share was seen as a fair return to shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivables growth accelerate in FY27 or only FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No asset growth guidance was given; management reiterated that asset growth will follow card acquisition at 0.9-1.0 million per quarter.

risks_watch: Revolver ratio (22%) drifting lower; instalment book offset is not expected to fully compensate; NIM at risk from cost-of-funds rise.
Receivables growth at ~2% YoY; no guidance given on asset growth.
Opex and cost-to-income: Q4 adjusted cost-to-income near 60% after one-offs; FY27 guidance 55-58%.
Geopolitical and macro uncertainty affecting credit cost moderation and the pace of ECL model refresh.
Q4 YoY instalment decline and loss of Apple offer; management called these transient, within 3-6 months.
Recovery pool (~INR190 crore) and write-offs trending lower; not disclosed in size.
543066|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability trends, but cautious and non-committal on growth, cost of funds and revolver mix, repeatedly declining to quantify FY27 asset growth and cost of funds.
key_quotes: Overall, the business is profitable, but the margins are comparatively thinner, which basically boost both on the cost and the income side.
So we are building on card acquisition, and we expect that the asset growth will follow the card acquisition growth.
We are underleveraged actually, if you look at that.
we are aiming towards 4% to 4.5% of ROA in the medium term. And that is achievable and we are working towards it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Credit cost expected to moderate further (Q4 gross credit cost 7.7%, down 55 bps QoQ) and ROA target 4-4.5% medium term, but NIM guided stable and cost-to-income 55-58% (FY26 55.3%) leaves little room for expansion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Card acquisition of ~917,000 new accounts in Q4 with next quarter expected in a similar 0.9-1.0 million range, but receivables only ~2% YoY and no asset growth guidance given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plans, capacity or utilisation data discussed; only AI/ML investment mentioned with no amount or timeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Only stable NIM, moderating credit cost and cost-to-income held at 55-58%; no revenue or receivables growth guidance, and receivables grew only ~2% YoY to INR56,926 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revolver rate (22%) drifting lower and NIM at risk from cost-of-funds rise (Q4 cost of funds 6.4%, ~70-75% of borrowings floating), with FY27 cost-to-income guided at 55-58% versus FY26 55.3% and Q4 near 60% adjusted.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches discussed beyond instalment lending as an offset to revolver decline.

rows.label: Instalment lending as revolver offset
rows.why: Management leaning on instalment lending to offset revolver rate drift from 22-24%, though it is not expected to fully compensate and Q4 instalment saw a YoY decline.

rows.label: Underleveraged balance sheet with 25.5% CAR
rows.why: CAR 25.5% and management calls the company underleveraged, implying headroom for faster growth if acquisition converts into receivables, but no growth guidance was given.

rows.label: Corporate-spend passback costs normalise
rows.why: Management said cost-to-income guided at 55-58% as passback costs normalise after FY26 opex rose 22% YoY, with Q4 cost-to-income at 57.2%.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 2.41%, credit cost 7.7%) and profitability, but cautious and non-committal on receivables growth, cost of funds and revolver mix, declining to quantify FY27 asset growth; analysts pressed on revolver downside and growth.

543066|2026-06.headline: SBI Cards Q1 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR664 crores on a sharp fall in credit cost to 6.5% gross, while revenue grew only 3%.
543066|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 profit grew on lower credit costs rather than revenue, with total revenue of INR5,205 crores up 3% YoY and gross credit cost down 301 bps YoY to 6.5%. Card spends hit a record INR1,18,475 crores (up 27% YoY) and spend market share rose to 19.5%, but receivables grew only about 2% QoQ and 3% YoY to INR58,269 crores. Management said asset growth should pick up from H2 FY27 and that cost of funds, stable at 6.6% this quarter, is expected to trend higher. Gross NPA fell to 2.04% and net NPA to 0.83%, the lowest since Q3 FY23.

segments.name: Retail cards
segments.commentary: Retail spends INR94,033 crores, up 14% YoY; online contributed 63% of retail spend and UPI on credit card usage grew 13% QoQ. Interest-earning assets stable at about 55%, revolver rate 22%.

segments.name: Corporate cards
segments.commentary: Corporate spend share was 20.33% of total spend this quarter, down from 21.92% last quarter; management targets about 20% and says corporate card profitability is very low.

segments.name: EMI / instalment lending
segments.commentary: EMI book stated at about 33% of portfolio per analyst question; management gave no numerical guidance but expects an uptick in festive season.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term ROA guidance of 4% to 4.5% reiterated; management says current trajectory (3.9% in Q1) puts it on track.
Gross credit cost expected to stay within the current range, subject to Middle East conflict impact; no numerical guidance given, but moderation expected.
Asset growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27 on higher acquisitions and festive season in Q3.
Cost of funds expected to trend higher in line with market rates; management also said cost of funds should remain in a similar range near term and depends on T-bill rates.
FY27 cost-to-income ratio expected in the range of about 56% to 58% (annual average).
NIM expected to stay around current levels (10.8%); revolver rates expected to stay stable.
Overlay of INR70 crores retained in Stage 1 for geopolitical uncertainty; INR65 crores released on improved portfolio mix.
Instalment-based (instance) fee income expected to rise in H2 on base effect; late fee income to stay at current level.
capex_capacity: Cards in force about 2.26 crores, up 7% YoY; more than 1 million new accounts added in Q1 FY27 (+17% YoY); net card addition of 4.84 lakh, highest in industry for the quarter per RBI data.
Sourcing split about 47% Banca and 53% open market.
Annual ECL model review completed in Q1: INR180 crores of the INR220 crores overlay consumed, INR65 crores released; INR70 crores overlay retained in Stage 1.
Write-back of INR35 crores on account of good asset quality this quarter, per management presentation.
Capital adequacy ratio 25.6%; liquidity described as strong.
demand_pricing: Spend market share rose to 19.5% (RBI June 2026 data) from 18.1% in FY26; market share in cards in force is 18.6%.
Strong spend categories: consumer durables, furnishing and hardware, apparel and jewellery; UPI on credit card growing with RuPay and QR acceptance.
Management says retail spending remains strong into Q2 despite monsoon concerns; festive season still ahead.
Rental transactions reopened only where acquirers have KYC'd landlords; volumes minimal and management is not pursuing rental fee income.
Management noted entry rates into the first delinquency bucket are near decadal lows.
Analyst cited a competitor expecting credit cost near 5% by Q3; management declined to endorse normalisation levels, saying moderation will continue.
Personal loans on credit card: management said it is not currently offering PL to new customers and is internally evaluating it.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for revolver trend and EMI share growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Revolver rates expected to stay stable in a similar range after a slight downward bias; no numerical guidance on EMI share, but an uptick expected with festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company offer personal loans via cards and how is the EMI share being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Some existing customers carry PL assets, but new PL offering is paused; the company is evaluating it internally. EMI push relies on pay-in-EMI in the app, OEM and PG tie-ups, and a rise in durables prices.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance for exit of FY27 and receivables growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance; credit cost expected to moderate further and receivables to grow in H2 FY27. Management declined to give absolute or percentage numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Relative economics of retail vs corporate spends?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate spends targeted at around 20% (industry 20-25%); corporate cards have no lending, earn only interchange and fees, and have very low profitability versus retail.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the QoQ rise in employee opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to higher past service cost provision from the new wage code liability.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be held or improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields to be kept in a broad range; levers include higher credit lines for instalment customers, and cost of funds increases pass through to incremental book.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL model refresh give tailwind next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Model will not be relaxed; any gains come from data refresh as asset quality improves, with ECL release already occurring.

qa_highlights.question: Stress in IT/salaried segments in South India?
qa_highlights.answer: No cohort stress seen in the book, including separate IT-sector analysis; monitoring continues despite reports of higher delinquencies at other lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Cost-to-income outlook for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year cost-to-income expected at about 56% to 58% as an average of four quarters; festive quarter will be higher.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given rate pause?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM expected to stay around current levels; cost of funds managed through source and pricing choices.

risks_watch: Cost of funds expected to rise with market rates, pressuring NIM from 10.8% if yields do not keep pace.
Middle East conflict and fuel price/inflation second-order effects on customer cash flows; management says no substantial impact seen yet.
Receivables growth only 3% YoY; growth recovery is guided to H2 FY27 and depends on acquisition quality and festive season.
Competitive pressure from NBFC consumer-durable loans and personal loans cannibalising card EMI and spend.
Opex rising QoQ with festive season; cost-to-income guided at 56-58% for FY27.
Monsoon impact on retail spend and whether the INR70 crore Stage 1 overlay is released.

543066|2026-09.headline: SBI Card Q2 FY27 PAT rose 75% YoY to INR778 crore on lower credit costs, while spend growth was just 3% and NIM is guided range-bound around 10.8%.
543066|2026-09.overview: SBI Card reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR5,141 crore (up 4% YoY) and PAT of INR778 crore (up 75% YoY), driven mainly by lower credit costs. Gross credit cost fell to 5.6% (down 98 bps QoQ and 342 bps YoY) and gross NPA to 1.9%. Total spends grew about 3% YoY to INR1,10,689 crore, with retail spends up 6% to a record INR95,299 crore, and management attributed the weak headline to festive timing shifting into Q3. Management expects receivables to grow from Q3 and retail spend growth of mid-teens to high-teens for FY27, but gave no receivables growth guidance. NIM was 10.8% with cost of funds up 18 bps QoQ to 6.8%, and management expects NIM to be range-bound as rate hikes feed in.

financial_highlights.metric: Daily weighted average cost of funds

segments.name: Retail spends
segments.commentary: Record INR95,299 crore in Q2, up 6% YoY; online was 62.8% of retail spend in H1 FY27. UPI spends on credit cards grew 17% QoQ, with INR21,300 crore of spends through UPI this quarter.

segments.name: Corporate spends
segments.commentary: INR15,390 crore in Q2, down QoQ; management says corporate is opportunistic, kept below 20% of total spend, and some spends were let go for margin reasons.

segments.name: Cards in force and acquisition
segments.commentary: Cards in force about 2 crore (32 lakh), up 8% YoY; more than 1 million new accounts added in Q2, up 18% YoY, with 49% from Banca and 51% from open market. Net addition of 8.6 lakh cards in FY27 to August.

guidance_outlook: Retail spend growth expected in the mid-teens to high-teens range for FY27 (management referenced a 14-16% range).
Receivables growth expected to start in H2 FY27 and from Q3; no numerical receivables growth guidance given.
NIM expected to be range-bound; cost of funds expected to rise over the next few quarters, with a possible further ~50 bps repo hike, impact expected to lag as the book reprices in about 60-75 days.
Gross credit cost expected around 6% for FY27 (management comfortable with 5.5%-6%), subject to geopolitical impact; management overlay of INR100 crore held.
Cost-to-income ratio guided at 57%-59% for FY27; no FY28 guidance given.
Quarterly run rate of more than 1 million new accounts to be maintained; Q3 opex expected to rise with festive spends.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capital expenditure figures, or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the transcript contains no capacity or utilisation metrics for the business.
Operating cost was INR2,649 crore in Q2 FY27, up 7% YoY and flat QoQ; management attributed the flat run-rate to investment in business growth, with Q3 opex expected to rise on festive spends.

Cost-to-income ratio was 58.7% in Q2 (up 193 bps YoY); guidance for FY27 is 57%-59%. No FY28 cost-to-income guidance was given (management: 'Not as of now' for next year, aiming to reduce it if possible).
demand_pricing: Festive season started around 11 October 2026 versus 22 September 2025 last year, which management cites as the main reason for the weak YoY spend comparison.
EMI offtake is rising as mobile phone prices increase; point-of-sale EMI subvention moved from around 16% to 16.5-17% over recent months, and conversion-to-EMI rates were also raised.
Interchange income rose in Q2 as networks increased rates on certain categories; management says the higher level is sustainable within a range.
Revolver rate at 22% and interest-earning assets stable at 55%; EMI share of book at 33%, revolvers 22% of book, and 45% of portfolio is transactor.
Co-brand additions: Google Pay Flex SBI Card and Advantage SBI Card on YONO; Eternal co-brand card launched; existing co-brands include Tata Neu, PhonePe, Google Pay, Flipkart and BPCL.

qa_highlights.question: Will spends and receivables inflect in Q3, and how long will it take for spend growth to reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that receivables growth starts in H2, from Q3. Spend growth is expected in the mid-teens to high-teens for FY27. Early festive EMI conversion trends are described as encouraging, but still early.

qa_highlights.name: How will NIM evolve given higher cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are optimising borrowing mix (working capital loans about 70-80 bps cheaper than CP), raising yields on the EMI book and converting transactors to EMI. Yield hikes are already in place, and management expects NIM to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6% credit cost guidance conservative given 5.5% run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 credit cost was 6.05%. Management sees 5.5%-6% as a comfortable range and does not expect credit costs to moderate much beyond that. The INR30 crore was a management overlay, not a provision.

qa_highlights.question: Why did corporate spends dip, and does opex stay in line?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate spends were let go for margin reasons. Opex was flat QoQ, but investment in growth was cited, and Q3 opex is expected to rise with festive spends. Cost-to-income guidance of 57%-59% is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CIF bank share rise to 46%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% of the portfolio was reclassified after a granular review of account features and channels. Management said the previous quarter would have shown the same bank versus open-market split on the new basis.

risks_watch: Rate pressure: repo hike already done, with another ~50 bps expected; borrowing mix and EMI repricing must offset cost of funds to hold NIM at 10.8%.
Geopolitical and macro risk (West Asia conflict, energy prices, inflation) could raise credit costs; INR100 crore management overlay is held.
Receivables growth is still unguided; transactor share (45%) can move quickly and affect IEA and yield.
Opex and cost-to-income could drift up from Q3 with festive spending and customer acquisition.
Fee income and the regulatory focus on fee cuts across lenders; management says interchange grows with spends and instance-based fees with CIF.

543187|2026-03.headline: Hitachi Energy India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 46.2% YoY to Rs 2,754.1 Cr, with record order backlog of Rs 29,555 Cr at FY26 end.
543187|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 orders were Rs 2,422.5 Cr (up 10.6% YoY) and revenue was Rs 2,754.1 Cr (up 46.2% YoY), with PAT of Rs 330.5 Cr. For FY26, revenue reached Rs 8,147.7 Cr (up 27.6%) and PAT Rs 987.8 Cr (up 157.3%), while FY26 orders were broadly flat at Rs 18,456.5 Cr (up 1.6%). Management highlighted completion of the 1,000 MW Mumbai City infeed HVDC project and a new Rs 2,000 Cr capex approval, taking cumulative capex to nearly Rs 4,000 Cr. Analyst questions focused on weak non-HVDC domestic orders, export mix, margins, and royalty.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: HVDC revenue in FY26 was about Rs 1,100 Cr, roughly 15% of Rs 8,000 Cr total revenue, per CEO and CFO; management says it is margin-accretive but not yet substantial. The 1,000 MW Mumbai City infeed (VSC) project was commissioned in FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue was about 25% of FY26 revenue and export orders are in a similar range, though lower in Q4 due to large domestic orders; management cites a 25-30% average, with a 3-pronged model (allocated markets, global feeder factory products like 66 kV breakers and COMBIFLEX relays, and component contract manufacturing).

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Q4 services orders were high, driven by a control and protection upgrade for MSETCL in India. Management named strengthening India services as a key pillar.

segments.name: Transmission / Transformers
segments.commentary: Transmission order intake showed a small dip in FY26 due to mismatch in large order values versus FY25. Management says the transformer pipeline is very strong and the temporary slowdown is behind them.

segments.name: Data centers, renewables, industry
segments.commentary: Order intake grew across industry, data centers, railways and renewables in FY26. Management says data centers are under 2 GW in India today, with a projected 6-9x expansion; Hitachi targets about 15% of data center capex as addressable.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward-looking numbers; CEO said 'we don't give any forward-looking numbers going forward' when asked about FY27 domestic non-HVDC order inflow.
Pipeline described qualitatively as very strong across renewables, data centers, transmission and transformers, excluding HVDC; industries described as intermittent but recovering.

HVDC: management said there is no capacity limitation to take more HVDC projects in the coming year or year after; at least 3, if not 4, HVDC projects expected in the pipeline over the next 2 years, with both LCC and VSC.

543212|2026-03.headline: Borosil FY26 revenue rose 8% to INR1,195.9 crore but operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore as Hydra flask supply disruption from the BIS QCO hit margins.
543212|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR1,195.9 crore (up 8% from INR1,107.8 crore), while pre-exceptional operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore and margin fell to 15.1% from 16.3%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.2% to INR284.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.2%, with the West Asia LPG supply disruption temporarily shutting the borosilicate and opal glass furnaces. Management attributed the Hydra shortfall to BIS/QCO-related supply chain problems and said the company is adding in-house flask capacity and solar power to offset cost pressures. Net debt at consolidated level was INR49.7 crore at FY26 end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins fall in Q4 despite borosilicate ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Chinese dumping, which Borosil can only partly offset with brand premium, plus higher gas and raw material costs in Q4. A price increase was taken but its impact lags.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA saving from solar?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Anand Sultania estimated about INR28 crore at EBITDA level for FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 90-95%. Growth has slowed, and only debottlenecking is planned. No major opalware capex; focus is on other categories.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes of 8-10% are enough to cover cost inflation, with 1-2 quarters of lag.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 10% gross margin improvement, but only after 6-12 months of stabilisation, so not in the first couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund rising debt and capex?

Hydra flask recovery depends on the in-house plant ramp-up; margin benefit is delayed 6-12 months.

543212|2026-09.headline: Borosil H1 FY27 revenue rose 8.8% to INR 627.4 crore and gross margin expanded 390 bps to 65.2%, helped by price hikes, mix and solar savings.
543212|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 8.8% YoY to INR 627.4 crore, with gross profit up 15.6% to INR 408.9 crore and EBITDA (excluding other income) up 20.5% to INR 107.7 crore. PAT improved to INR 44.7 crore from INR 40.1 crore. Management credited calibrated price increases of roughly 2.5-7% across categories, better mix, operational efficiencies and captive solar savings, partly offset by West Asia-linked input cost inflation. Glassware growth was muted (2.7%) because the Diwali shift moved B2B demand, while non-glassware grew 10.9% and Opalware 7.8%. DGTR issued final findings on 24 September 2026 recommending five-year anti-dumping duty on Chinese borosilicate glassware, pending Ministry of Finance notification.

Solar phase 3 gives about INR 30 crore annual EBITDA savings; phase 4 adds about INR 12 crore per annum from Q4 FY27 (INR 16-17 crore of phase 1-2 savings already in FY26).

Further price hikes depend on evolution of gas and LPG costs; last price increase was taken at end of Q1/start of Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Two double-wall Hydra lines in Rajasthan (Stylenest India) commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line delayed from December 2026 to January 2027 due to port congestion. Both lines already above 80% utilisation.

Captive solar at Bikaner: 35.8 MWp commissioned in three phases with 16.9 MWh BESS; solar now meets about 60% of power requirements. Additional 6.5 MWp with 5.0 MWh BESS (INR 27.6 crore) under implementation; 3.0 MWp for Hydra (INR 10.0 crore) expected in Q4 FY27.
Borosilicate Pressware furnace expansion at Jaipur from 25 TPD to 32 TPD with a third forming line, capex INR 50 crore, commissioning by end of Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation is 90%.
New glassware facility at Bharuch will be set up and funded by Borosil Scientific Ltd instead of Borosil, subject to approvals.
Solar phase 4 capex of about INR 37 crore to follow.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 2.5-3% in Opalware in some ranges, 3-5% in some ranges and 5-7% in others, effective from Q2 FY27.
Management said October 2026 showed good momentum across categories and channels, with trade and B2B strong, followed by e-commerce and LFS, and new premium products well received.

Working capital rose about 20-25 days YoY at September, which management attributed mainly to Diwali timing and inventory built up from dumped imports and BIS challenges. Management said the inventory should be read on a March-to-March basis.
Management said non-glassware growth was not mainly restocking; channel inventory was built partly from low vacuum-bottle capacity earlier.
Management said Borosil competes on quality and differentiation rather than price, citing a 25%+ CAGR in the appliances category.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biggest execution risk in moving toward appliances, and how will margins and share be protected against price undercutting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appliances are not growing at the cost of glassware, that glass is still a market-adoption category, and that Borosil competes on quality, not price.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk to margins once the Diwali-related lift fades, and which external cost pressures matter most?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LPG and raw-material pressure eased from Q1 to Q2, price pass-through improved and solar phase 3 savings will support sustained margins, but future gas-cost increases remain undecided.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the solar savings is in the numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 3 gives about INR 30 crore annual EBITDA savings (incremental INR 13 crore over FY26), with a further INR 12 crore from phase 4 from Q4 FY27. Q2 expenses were about 5.3% of sales vs 7.2% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR 1.2 crore government grant in cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a capital subsidy on Opalware and borosilicate furnace expansions, not revenue. Total incentive is about INR 55 crore, with the balance to be received in future years and deducted from fixed assets.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the YoY gross margin rise and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price increases, efficiency and cost actions, and Hydra double-wall lines. It declined to quantify the split beyond the Opalware 2.5-3% price increase.

qa_highlights.question: When will the anti-dumping duty take effect and what is the financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The Ministry of Finance has about 90 days from 24 September 2026, so by about 24 December. Management said there is no direct margin or pricing benefit; the main effect is lower inventory and better growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the stainless-steel third double-wall line and when will its margin benefit show?
qa_highlights.answer: The third line slipped about a month to January 2027 due to port congestion, with some impact expected from end Q4 FY27 after stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for inventory reduction and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not give a number; sales are being drawn from year-1 and year-2 inventory built for a larger market, and focus is on volume growth to bring inventory down.

543213|2026-03.headline: Rossari Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 684.9 crore (+18% YoY), but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% from 12.7%.
543213|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and absolute EBITDA, with revenue up 18% YoY to Rs 684.9 crore and EBITDA up 11% to Rs 77.3 crore, though margin slipped to 11.3% from 12%. For FY26, revenue grew 15% (volume-driven) to Rs 2,396.4 crore while EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 286 crore. March saw raw material price increases of 25-30% that compressed gross margin, and management says these are now being passed through from April. Management rephased the Rs 192 crore capex plan across Rossari, Unitop and Tristar, guided FY27 growth of at least 15% and consolidated EBITDA margin of 12-13%, and flagged plans to exit non-core consumer and institutional businesses.

rows.why: Pharma is a new focus area expected to carry the highest gross margin once scaled, with an FY27 pharma facility and aroma chemicals project in the Rs 50-75 crore capex, and AHN premix revenue ramp from Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Debt-free in ~18 months (aim)
rows.why: Management targets becoming debt-free within 18 months but said 'the time will tell'; capex cut to Rs 50-75 crore for FY27 frees cash, while divestment of non-core office space has no committed value or timeline (one to two years).

rows.label: Institutional and B2C breakeven in FY27
rows.why: Management expects breakeven or profitability in FY27 with losses moderating in H2 FY26, but B2C revenue is only Rs 250-260 crore on about 90 days of working capital and the target is not yet demonstrated.

rows.label: Raw material pass-through from April 2026
rows.why: Raw materials rose 25-30% in March and management says increases are being passed through from April 1, easy for most products but resisted in textiles, the key test for the 12-13% margin guide.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the Q4 record and the at-least-15% FY27 growth target, but cautious on the Middle East and raw material environment and the 12-13% margin; analysts pushed on the capex cut, the Reliance EO timing, segment margins and divestment values, which management left vague.

543213|2026-06.headline: Rossari Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 697.2 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.6% from 12.5%.
543213|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 697.2 crore (up 28% YoY) and EBITDA hit a record Rs 80.6 crore (up 18.7%), though margin fell to 11.6% from 12.5%. Core B2B EBITDA was Rs 85 crore (up 13%, ~14% margin), with the institutional and B2C businesses dragging margins and remaining flat in growth. PAT was Rs 35.1 crore (up 4.5%). Management is pursuing non-core asset monetisation, B2C exits and product-mix changes, and says Rs 11.6% is the margin base; target is ~15% EBITDA margin in about two years. Raw material spikes, phenol losses of about Rs 5 crore and freight volatility weighed on the quarter.

segments.name: HPPC
segments.commentary: Crossed Rs 550 crore quarterly revenue, growing ~28% YoY; new products such as NMMO, MDEA, spray-cooled powders, biosurfactants and fibre finishes are contributing.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals (TSC)
segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; new Fibre Chemicals Division launched during the quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health and Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; vitamin premix plant now operational; trace minerals and enzyme premixes added. Pharma revenue was above Rs 50 crore last year and is guided to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Growth flat YoY; losses moderated. Institutional EBITDA margin cited at 13.6% vs ~16% last year. Debt in this business about Rs 50 crore; exit of consumer/B2C portion planned, institutional cleaning retained.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of around 15% reiterated on an annualised basis, though management said quarterly prediction is becoming difficult.
Management says 11.6% EBITDA margin should be the base level; steady-state EBITDA margin target of at least 15%, expected in about two years.
Pharma revenue potential of Rs 30-50 crore in the second half of FY27 (Q2/Q3 compliance target), per analyst question on the Rs 70-75 crore figure.
Finance cost guided at Rs 9-10 crore per quarter run-rate going forward (Q1 interest about Rs 11 crore).
EO supply expected by around December 2026; FY28 expected to be better with a full year of additional EO.
Saudi Arabia project: about 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products; still in survey and feedstock/land allocation stage.

New R&D centre commissioned in Q4 FY26 and ramping up.

Saudi Arabia: initial operational and pre-operational spends only; capex not finalised.

Pass-through of raw material price increases is achieved, but frequent up/down moves create buyer uncertainty; freight and vessel availability cost margin.
Phenol loss of about Rs 5 crore in Q4 FY26 due to delayed China shipments (noted as Q1 context by management); one-off RM block purchase also hurt the quarter; prices now back to earlier levels.
Growth shifted to non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM); agro demand subdued but non-EO agro inputs grew.
Single EO supplier in India, priced on world EO price; limited negotiating power.
Freight rates rose again after brief easing; new orders taken at higher freight.

qa_highlights.question: What margin improvement path and timing for EBITDA margin, given flat margins over 4-5 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Sablok said 11.6% is close to last quarter and slightly below last year; margins to improve as utilisation rises, low-margin exits and pharma/aroma mix shift. Wait-and-see for at least two quarters due to pricing and RM pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is 11.6% the base margin and what is steady-state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11.6% should be the base level. Base business ex-B2C is 14-15%; target is around 15% steady-state EBITDA margin within two years after B2C recalibration and asset monetisation.

qa_highlights.question: Exit of B2C business: investment, debt and margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate investment as assets are shared (Silvassa). Debt in institutional/B2C about Rs 50 crore. Exit releases at least 2-3% EBITDA margin. Institutional cleaning retained; only consumer/B2C exits.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing vs volume growth and growth levers without EO availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume ~10% YoY, rest from pricing. Growth from new non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM), trace minerals, vitamin and enzyme premixes; pharma to rise to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic-focused peers gain while Rossari did not?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-molecule producers benefited; specialty players absorbed raw material hits. Phenol shipment delay from China cost about Rs 5 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi Arabia project timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Survey and feedstock/land allocation still in progress; nothing finalised. About 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost rise and average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest because term loans for capex were capitalised earlier and are now expensed as assets commissioned; run-rate to be Rs 9-10 crore per quarter.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on B2C exits, asset monetisation and utilisation; management declined to guide quarterly numbers.
EO supply (single Indian supplier) expected only by about December 2026; EO-linked growth is delayed.
Raw material and freight volatility linked to West Asia/geopolitics; freight rates rose again after easing.
Thailand and Saudi Arabia ramp-up and pre-operative costs weigh on margins.
Pharma compliance timeline (Q2/Q3) gates the Rs 30-50 crore H2 revenue potential.
Interest costs rising as capitalised projects go into P&L; watch whether run-rate falls to Rs 9-10 crore.

543213|2026-09.headline: Rossari Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 697.6 crore, a record, with EBITDA of Rs 87 crore (12.5% margin).
543213|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set record revenue (Rs 697.6 crore, +19% YoY) and EBITDA (Rs 87 crore, +21% YoY), with growth led by volume and value-added products. Gross margin was 31.6%, up about 200 bps QoQ on product mix, but core B2B EBITDA margin fell to 14.1% from 14.8% YoY on freight and raw material costs. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to about 12% and revenue growth to mid-to-high teens, while citing uncertainty from the Middle East situation. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore and working capital days improved to 86 from 97 at FY26 end.

segments.name: HPPC (Home, Personal Care & Industrial)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 541.9 crore, +18% YoY; H1 Rs 1,095.1 crore, +20% (H1 growth 24% per Sunil Chari). Growth led by personal care, agro surfactants, adjuvants and oil & gas; ethylene oxide constraints limited ethoxylate volumes and sequential revenue was broadly flat.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 120.8 crore, +26% YoY and about +14% QoQ; H1 Rs 226.9 crore, +24%. Driven by exports to Bangladesh, Southeast Asia, Turkey and Latin America, plus the Thailand facility and the new fibre chemicals division.

segments.name: Animal Health & Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 34.8 crore, +11% YoY; H1 Rs 72.8 crore, +19%. Q2 is seasonally the weakest quarter; management expects Q3 and Q4 to peak.

segments.name: Core B2B (ex institutional and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 619.9 crore, +21% YoY; EBITDA Rs 87.2 crore, +15% YoY, margin 14.1% vs 14.8% in Q2 FY26 and 13.5% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 77.7 crore, +3% YoY; EBITDA +Rs 0.2 crore vs loss of Rs 3.7 crore in Q2 FY26, after portfolio rationalisation. Management targets positive EBITDA in H2 and for full FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 12% plus/minus; management expects margin improvement only from FY28.
FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens to high-teens, down from the 12-14% initial view, given demand and logistics uncertainty.
Peak utilisation of the new ethoxylation facility at Dahej expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28; peak sales target remains 3x capex value.
Working capital days expected to stay in the 87-90 day range by end-March 2027.
Working capital debt expected to be repaid by about mid-2027; all cash flows to go to debt reduction for now.
Exports targeted at 30%+ of revenue by end of this year (Q2 export share 31%, H1 27%).
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 60%; new ethoxylation facility (Dahej) at about 30% and ramping; full healthy utilisation expected by next year as Reliance EO capacity arrives.
Reliance ethylene oxide expansion expected in Q1 FY28; no confirmed incremental EO allocation yet, with confirmation hoped for in the next couple of months.
Capital work in progress was Rs 156 crore at 30 September; about Rs 50-75 crore more capex in H2 FY27, with most projects closing by end-2026 and no major capex in India in the following year.
Remaining projects cover pharma excipients, aroma chemicals, hydrogenation and biosurfactant expansion; no volume figures disclosed yet.

Saudi Arabia: Board approved leasing land to wholly owned subsidiary Rossari International Limited Company for a greenfield plant; early site work (fencing, boundary wall) in coming months. Project details, capex and timelines to come after Board approval, likely in 8-12 months.
Thailand blending facility ramping up for Southeast Asia customers; EXCiPACT registration obtained for the Unitop plant.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth was mostly volume-driven; some product prices were cut as raw material prices eased early in the quarter.
Freight costs roughly doubled to tripled versus last year; not all customers absorb the full freight increase. Phenol and other core raw materials are higher YoY.
Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and about 35% QoQ in Q2; export share 31% of revenue; H1 export share 27%.
Pharma exports were about Rs 50 crore last year; qualification takes 6 months to 2 years, and management expects strong growth this year.
Oil and gas focus markets are India, the Middle East, and Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan; US sales go through distributors with no segment data.
Management declined to give a specific H2 revenue outlook, citing the Middle East situation, shipping routes and container and ISO tank availability.

qa_highlights.question: Where is export growth coming from and what is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and 35% QoQ, driven by HPPC and textiles in Southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America, with Thailand helping. Target is 30%+ of revenue from exports by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity ramp-up and peak revenue at the new Dahej ethoxylation plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak utilisation is expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28. The 3x capex-to-peak-sales target is unchanged. Utilisation is about 30% today.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core B2B margin fall YoY, and how will it recover above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs (doubled to tripled) and raw material inflation compressed margins. Some pass-through has been achieved, but freight recovery is still a challenge. No specific recovery date was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi Arabia project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board approved land leasing in KSA. Feasibility, feedstock and capex work is ongoing, and the next Board approval and detailed timelines are expected in 8-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin benefit from acquisitions such as Unitop and the move to value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unitop and Tristar had lower gross margins at acquisition, and in-house ethoxylation now requires advance raw material purchases, which lengthened working capital. Gross margin is better than at end-2021 when the three businesses are combined.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the working capital debt and the net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects working capital debt to be repaid by mid-2027. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore; H1 operating cash flow was about Rs 131 crore.

risks_watch: Ethylene oxide supply from Reliance is a constraint; the expansion is expected in Q1 FY28, but incremental allocation is not yet confirmed.
Freight and logistics costs are high because of Middle East and Red Sea/Hormuz disruptions, and the core B2B margin fell 70 bps YoY to 14.1%.
The FY27 margin guide of about 12% is below H1 levels of about 12%; the company has not given a clear margin path beyond FY27.
Institutional and B2C is only at breakeven, and plans to sell this business remain undetermined in timing and value.
ROCE has fallen to low teens and is expected to recover only from next year; the Saudi capex return profile is not yet disclosed.
AHN growth has slowed; the seasonal peak in Q3 and Q4 must deliver.

But we don't want to hazard any guess, give anything, which after 6 months, the investors will say, you said it, and you couldn't do it?
So probably next year, we should start seeing improvements in the EBITDA percentage.

543214|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin hit a record 11.90% on INR229.89 crore total income (+19% YoY); order book rose to INR650 crore.
543214|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR229.89 crore (+19% YoY), EBITDA INR27.36 crore (+25% YoY) at 11.90% margin, and PAT INR18.45 crore. For FY26, total income was INR825.45 crore (+15%), EBITDA INR93.57 crore (11.34% margin) and PAT INR61.94 crore (+16%). Order book at 31 March 2026 was INR650 crore, up from about INR450 crore at Q3, with the INR200 crore increase entirely from Maruti Suzuki new models. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, instead pointing to a long-term INR3,000 crore revenue ambition for FY30 that is only partly covered by the current order book.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; described as highest ever margin

financial_highlights.metric: ROCE (ex ROU, surplus cash and land)

financial_highlights.change: Revised consolidated cash flow filed 13 May after XBRL filing error
up from about INR450 crore at Q3 FY26; highest in company history

segments.name: Seat covers and frames (NDR Auto)
segments.commentary: NDR does seat covers and frames; Bharat Seats (investee, ~28% held by NDR) does seat assembly and foam. Current revenue run-rate cited as about INR830-850 crore.

segments.name: Hayashi JV (50:50)
segments.commentary: Sunshade business of about INR20 crore transferred to the JV; INR80 crore approved project cost with about INR30 crore invested so far. Production start delayed from April to June due to operational issues. Two small ambient lighting orders from Maruti Suzuki, expected INR10-20 crore revenue combined.

FY30 revenue ambition is INR3,000 crore for NDR standalone (excluding Bharat Seats), implying roughly INR500 crore from existing customers and products plus INR1,000 crore still to be won; updates promised by end of CY2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200 crore order book increase from new models or new OEMs, and what caused the Hayashi JV start delay?
qa_highlights.answer: All new Maruti Suzuki models; eVitara removed from the book as it entered production. The JV start moved about two months to June because of operational issues, not capex delay.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses rose from INR21 crore to INR24 crore QoQ; were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the rise reflects higher project and marketing expenses including R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11.5% EBITDA margin sustainable, and what margin range applies as new products ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current margin is sustainable and gave no range for the ramp, citing start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much visibility is there to the INR3,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: INR500 crore is targeted from existing customers and products; the remaining INR1,000 crore needs more time, with an update promised by end of calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order visibility for the INR150 crore new-product capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Seat belt reminder, seat latch and seat insert orders are already held and will move to the new facilities, with production starting January 2027 and ramping slowly. Hayashi has two ambient lighting orders and the shade business.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow weak, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was positive at INR37.12 crore after a corrected filing on 13 May; about INR12 crore went to a Delhi office, INR6 crore supported subsidiaries and MSME vendor payables rose. Management expects normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 revenue or margin guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY27 and whether the Bharat Seats target changed?

543220|2026-03.headline: Max Healthcare Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 2,664 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 26.8% on chemo-drug discontinuation and higher ALOS.

qa_highlights.answer: Doctor hiring followed the 25-30% capacity addition in late 2024 and the current 20%+ brownfield rollout across Mohali, Nanavati, Smart and Lucknow. Management expects doctor cost ratios to decline with operating leverage. Kalinga will add manpower but will not move the needle.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Lucknow land bank and the Shaheed Path greenfield fit together, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gomti Nagar (27 acres) will reach 570 beds, with another 200-300 beds planned there. Shaheed Path (5+ acres) is a 700-bed phased project over about 3 years, expandable to about 900 beds. It is a multi-location cluster strategy rather than cannibalisation.

capex_capacity: Brownfield: over the last two quarters, phased commissioning of more than 20% additional brownfield capacity at Mohali, Nanavati (Mumbai) and Max Smart (Delhi); remaining beds to be operationalised over the next 2-3 months. Management also expects another ~10% capacity from the 500-bed Gurugram greenfield on commissioning.

Gurugram Sector 56 (500 beds): interior and facade works started; commissioning targeted by end of FY27 after slipping from earlier 'middle of second half' guidance, due to labour attrition during state elections, LPG shortage affecting contractor labour (company now serving meals to ~1,100-1,200 workers) and about a couple of months of delay. Initial operations expected at ~200 beds; breakeven targeted within FY28 (Dwarka precedent: 300 beds, started with 140, breakeven in 6 months vs 12-month guidance, H1 EBITDA loss ~INR 35 crore).

Max Lucknow Gomti Nagar: 426 beds currently, rising to 570 beds over the next 2 quarters; further 200-300 beds planned on the 27-acre Gomti Nagar land bank over time. Lucknow Shaheed Path: 700-bed greenfield approved at INR 1,400 crore, phased over ~3 years, expandable to ~900 beds; 5+ acres.

Pipeline (commissioning in next 2-3 years): Max Nagpur 100 beds by FY28; Zirakpur, Mohali 400 beds in FY28; Max Dwarka 260 beds (building plan submission underway, 24 months); Max Vaishali 200 beds (awaiting building plan approvals, 24 months post approval); Max Patparganj 400 beds with D-wall construction started, commissioning by FY29. Dwarka brownfield of 200-plus beds being planned; Dwarka oncology centre to start next month.

Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, 10-acre site): controlling stake acquired in May 2026, consolidation from Q1 FY27; about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA; plans to revamp and expand. Acquisition consideration not discussed.

FY26 capital deployment: INR 1,627 crore into ongoing expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, INR 131 crore for land at Vaishali, INR 146 crore dividend paid; Q4 deployment INR 328 crore.
demand_pricing: Network Q4 occupancy above 75% despite higher operational beds; OBDs up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; ALOS up 9% YoY due to simultaneous multi-location brownfield rollout, expected to tighten over time.

ARPOB INR 77,900 in Q4, after absorbing higher ALOS and discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients (CGHS). Oncology OBDs down ~5-6% YoY; oncology share of in-patient revenue 21% vs 26% in Q4 FY25 and 24% in Q3 FY26. Management expects oncology share to hover at 21-22%, not return to 25-26%.

Chemo-drug discontinuation: discontinued since October 2025; annual chemotherapy billing down ~INR 200 crore (gross); net of GST ~INR 140 crore. Earlier drugs were billed at MRP with ~15-16% margins; CGHS now requires ~30% discount to MRP. Management says this is industry-wide but Max is most affected given oncology and institutional mix. Q4 carries the full impact.

CGHS rate revision: ~INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates, at two hospitals so far) to flow over the coming months. Management said CGHS is reconsidering the chemo discount but timing is not fixed. ECHS and PSU patients lack dispensary access to drugs such as Keytruda.

Noida ramp-up: occupancy above 64-65% in Q4 with doctors hired; management says it is in line with expectations. Dwarka at 80-85% occupancy. Management cited a hockey-stick occupancy curve: units break even around 50-55% occupancy, and the real value comes from 60-65% to about 80%.

Other metrics: Max@Home revenue INR 73 crore (+30% YoY, 16 service lines, 15 cities); Max Lab revenue INR 52 crore (+14% YoY, 60+ cities, ~6 lakh patients); international patient revenue INR 227 crore (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital revenue); digital revenue INR 838 crore (~31% of revenue). Q4 doctor costs about INR 435 crore; management expects operating leverage from here.
Management stated the company sees 10-12% PAT margin as the industry's steady state. It said doctor compensation increases in micro-markets are transferred to patients over time.

AGEasy targeted for EBITDA breakeven by the last quarter of FY27; monthly exit revenue run rate of INR14-16 crores for FY27 indicated.

Estate 361 Phase 2 (remaining 180 units) launch announcement expected within days; company commits to 1.5 million sq ft in the project.
Management fee estimates: E360 about INR130 crores lifetime, E361 about INR200 crores lifetime, Noida Phase 1 about INR14 crores pending possession-linked payments.
capex_capacity: Care homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; 28 beds in one Gurgaon home under renovation, expected live soon; 5 of 7 mature homes tracking to the model, per management.
Care home target economics: ROCE of 25-26%, 32%+ contribution margin and 16-18% EBITDA margin at maturity; 50-bed home takes 8-10 quarters to reach 65-70% occupancy.
New bed additions to be explored in H2 FY27, with site search starting around October-November 2026 (6-9 months lead time).
Noida Phase 1: partial occupancy certificate received for 3 towers by ContendBuilders SPV; construction complete, about INR70-75 crores of pending finishing bills.
Noida Phase 2: about 440,000 sq ft (about 220 units) yet to be developed; re-approval of revised building plans required before sales.

Pipeline: Sector 105 Noida intergenerational project (1.1 million sq ft), 2 further opportunities (Bangalore and Dehradun); management says all three could total about 2 million sq ft. Chandigarh project lost height clearance post Operation Sindoor.
demand_pricing: Estate 361 Phase 1 sold 141 of 180 units by the call date; management said inventory is nearly exhausted for certain unit types.
Noida Phase 2 market pricing is 2-3x Phase 1 realisations, at about INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft per management, implying roughly INR700 crores-plus potential on the 440,000 sq ft remaining.
AGEasy RoAS: marketplaces about 1.0 at start of FY26, exit about 2.0; D2C from 0.7-0.8 to 1.7-1.8. Online gross margin 38% to 46%; 65% of 19 FY26 launches at 50%+ gross margin.

AGEasy COGS pressure from China sourcing (30% of sourcing) due to geopolitics; mitigated by alternate Indian vendors, larger pre-orders and small price increases. No significant margin impact in Q3 or Q4 per management.
Care home occupancy averaged lower because of new homes added in Q4; mature beds grew about 10% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: When will Estate 361 Phase 2 launch, and are residential collections lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 launch announcement expected within days as 140 of 180 units are sold; collections are lumpy, with booking fee of INR25 lakh, then 10% on application and another 10%, with construction-linked collections over about 3 quarters, lumpy in FY27 and more regular from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the management fee outlook for E360, E361 and Noida, and the direct cost?
qa_highlights.answer: E360 about INR130 crores and E361 about INR200 crores lifetime management fee; Noida about INR14 crores pending. Variable cost is about 15% of fee; post-completion annuity is about INR10-12 crores per 250-unit community (60% CAM, 40% discretionary).

qa_highlights.question: Will Noida Phase 2 start and how much is pending on Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 sales expected during FY27 after re-approval of building plans; about 440,000 sq ft remaining. Phase 1 construction complete, with INR70-75 crores of pending bills to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: Why no entry into Hyderabad and what is the status of partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Residence entry delayed by unlimited FSI which lets developers maximise density; assisted living in Hyderabad is on the list and to be examined later in FY27. boAt watch product has not taken off as expected, but tech solutions are being worked on; IIT partnership on wheelchairs is a major revenue contributor.

qa_highlights.question: Is AGEasy on track for INR500 crores revenue around FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects continued high growth year-on-year, similar to the past two years, without reiterating the INR500 crore target numerically.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn EBITDA and PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to show path to profitability for one or two verticals in later FY27; labour code and minimum wage revisions are a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new labour codes and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code impact is about INR3-4 crores across entities, mainly gratuity provisioning, recognised in FY27 as the code came in March 2026. Payroll is about INR80-90 crores; management said the reported top line excludes SPV sales.

qa_highlights.question: When is the fundraise and what about the INR32 crore tax demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Fundraise timing depends on market sentiment; cash comfortable for 3-6 months, with an update expected this year. The INR32 crore tax demand on Dehradun is being contested via rectification for unallowed brought-forward losses; if accepted, it reduces to nil.

risks_watch: Lumpy residential collections: FY27 expected to be lumpy, with EBITDA losses possible in some periods despite overall project profitability.
Funding: company cash cover quoted as 3-6 months; equity raise timing tied to market conditions and not yet executed.
Noida Phase 2 approvals are pending; Phase 1 SPV profitability reduced by cost escalation and only net profit is consolidated.
Care home occupancy on new beds and the 2H FY27 bed expansion plan; unit-level breakeven still 4-6 quarters away.
Input cost risk for AGEasy from China sourcing and geopolitics; minimum wage revisions and labour code impact on costs.
INR32 crore income tax demand on Dehradun pending rectification outcome.

key_quotes: We expect these numbers to further improve in the coming financial year. This will be a testimony to our commitment to demonstrate path to profitability in all our businesses.

This event also has a potential to unlock the receivables of upwards of INR150 crores and also gives us an opportunity now to re-file for approval of Phase 2, which also is a big unlock given the way the market has now matured, the price points are 2x, 3x of what we sold last time.

543223|2026-06.headline: Max India Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 66% YoY to INR68.6 crore, but EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore; AGEasy breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.
543223|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR41.3 crore a year ago, though it fell sequentially on lumpy DM fee income. The EBITDA loss was INR25 crore, against INR23.2 crore a year ago and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26, because Q4 included an exceptional DM fee. Antara Noida (340 units) received possession offers in June 2026, with about 75% of dues collected by the call date, though revenue recognition is deferred to Q2 on possession. Management said care home occupancy is improving at 5 of 8 homes and AGEasy's ARR is trending up toward INR120-150 crore, and it reiterated AGEasy profitability by around Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Antara Senior Living (residences)
segments.commentary: Dehradun is profitable and fully occupied; Estate 360 Gurgaon is fully sold out. E361 has sold 154 of 360 units by June end, with 27 sold in Q1 and about 34 in July. Noida possession offers went to 340 residents in June, with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 Care Homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; occupied bed days up 23% QoQ. Occupancy rose at Bannerghatta to 41% (from 37%), Gurugram to 41% (from 33%), Whitefield to 18% (from 8%) and OMR to 12% (from 3%). Four homes reached ARPOB above INR7,000 in June.

segments.name: AGEasy (consumer products)
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR19 crore in Q1, below INR23 crore in Q4 on post-peak moderation. Online gross margin held at 45% (vs 46%). Marketplace ROAS 3.8 and D2C exit ROAS 2.6; marketplace CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically. Monthly revenue run-rate about INR10 crore in July.

segments.name: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR15.75 lakh in Q1 with negative contribution margin; average revenue per client INR4,000, client satisfaction 96%, sessions rose from 199 to 307 in June. Will be built into residences and Care Homes, not as a standalone business.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy expected to reach contribution and EBITDA breakeven around Q4 FY27 (management: 'by January or last quarter of this year'), with CM2 improving as ROAS rises.
AGEasy revenue doubling target for FY27 (from INR77 crore to about INR150 crore) reiterated; management expects significant Q2-Q4 top-line improvement.
Management said it will report a smaller EBITDA loss next quarter versus the 63% figure cited for FY26 (loss to revenue ratio).

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.
Incremental capital requirement of about USD20 million over the next two years (reduced from about USD25 million), with the second fund raise deferred.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida (340 units): possession offers issued June 2026; residents expected to move in over 30-45 days; Phase II approval is the next step, with rates cited at INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft versus INR7,000-10,000 earlier.
Care Homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; all 8 operational after DLF Phase II Gurgaon relaunch in July 2026; each new bed costs about INR10-12 lakh including operating losses.
Chandigarh project unwound after height clearance denial near flight paths post Operation Sindoor.
Second tranche of preference issue of INR40 crore received in July 2026; management says the total capital need is unchanged but working-capital credit lines are being used to bridge timing.
demand_pricing: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity slowed in April-June amid geopolitical uncertainty but recovered in July (34 units) and August; management says it has not seen DLF's senior-living entry affect sales.
AGEasy ROAS improved to 2.0 at Q1 exit from 1.8 in Q4; conversion rate rose from 2% to 3.5% after brand spend (Anupam Kher as ambassador).
AGEasy repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); management's directional target is 20%+.
Management noted that logistics and China-sourcing disruption raised COGS and forced some airlifting, depressing margins.
Competition: management said real-estate developers and hospital chains can replicate infrastructure but not services IP; DLF's launch plans in Gurgaon are reportedly small and tied to Medanta.

qa_highlights.question: What should change in cost and top line by Q4 FY27 for the EBITDA breakeven target, and what are the Care Home bed-addition plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 numbers; breakeven commitment applies to AGEasy, while Care Homes need 8-10 quarters per bed to turn profitable. No new beds are being added now; expansion decision is timed for October-November 2026 subject to occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Blended ARPOB for Care Homes once occupancy rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended ARPOB should be near INR7,500 as recent bed additions were at higher rates.

qa_highlights.question: Bookkeeping: how much of Noida collections is recognised in Q1, and reconciliation of senior living income?
qa_highlights.answer: No Noida revenue was recognised in June; recognition is tied to possession, expected in Q2. Senior living income includes DM fee (about INR7 crore), Dehradun operations (about INR6 crore), finance lease income from re-leasing (about INR15 crore, treated as exceptional) and treasury income (about INR8 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Will AGEasy's INR77 crore to about INR150 crore revenue doubling plan hold given Q1 revenue of INR18-19 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the plan; July run-rate reached about INR120 crore annualised, with Q2-Q4 expected to show significant top-line improvement as ROAS improves.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 AGEasy revenue was seasonal, and what are repeat rate and CAC/LTV indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited festive (Sep-Oct) and winter seasonality plus marketplace year-end deals. Repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); the directional target is 20%+, and ROAS (marketplace near 4, D2C 2.5) is used as the efficiency metric.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from hospital chains, developers and financial players, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued services and IP, not infrastructure, are the moat; hospitals would dilute margins in Care Homes; for AGEasy, moats are senior-specific products (3 patents granted, 3 filed) and brand. AGEasy market potential seen at about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which business gives highest ROCE, and expected cash burn for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: AGEasy expected to have the highest ROCE, followed by Care Homes (about 23-24%+). Management declined to give FY27-28 projections; it said the EBITDA loss ratio fell from 95% to 63% and will fall further next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Capital plan and incremental requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capital need unchanged for two years, reduced from about USD25 million to under USD20 million; incremental requirement about USD20 million. Second fund raise deferred using credit lines; INR40 crore second pref tranche received in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DLF's senior living entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DLF's Gurgaon plan is a small addition within an existing township, reportedly tied to Medanta, and has had no visible impact on Gurgaon sales velocity; it welcomes more players for category awareness.

AGEasy perhaps by January or last quarter of this year will be in that zone.
So we are not building a INR10,000 crores business in AGEasy in the next 5 years.
But the total number of capital required has not changed for the last 2 years.

543223|2026-09.headline: Max India consolidated revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR 95.5 crores in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA loss halved to INR 11.4 crores.

EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 11.4 crores from INR 25.3 crores a year ago and INR 24.9 crores in Q1, a 55% YoY and 54% QoQ reduction. Management attributed the improvement to higher revenue and cost optimisation, while flagging that the assisted senior living (ASL) DM fee income is lumpy and tied to construction-linked collections. Noida Phase 1 handovers accelerated to over 200 units, and AGEasy hit its highest-ever monthly revenue of INR 14.9 crores in September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How much of AGEasy's September surge is seasonal versus sustainable, and why did offline revenue jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishaan Khanna said 75-80% of the surge is sustainable, with some festive-driven rationalisation expected in October. Offline growth comes from expanded distributor networks built over the last 3 quarters, and Q3 is expected to exceed Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Where will employee costs stabilise, and what drives operational expenses for assisted care?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta said employee cost rose from Noida staffing (150+ added) and the labour code and revised PF rules, which were unanticipated. Ajay Agrawal said corporate employee cost is stable, and variable costs rise only with new projects, geographies or care homes. Ankit Kalra said assisted care opex covers care home operations and AGEasy logistics and marketplace commissions.

qa_highlights.question: How is the DM fee revenue recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Agrawal said the fee is accrued on collections made by Max Estates, reconciled quarterly, at 9.5% of collections net of pass-through and brokerage, and recognised when the invoice is raised, not at project completion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state ARPOB, and what drives it?

For FY26, revenue was INR714.52 crore (up 80%), EBITDA INR83.78 crore (margin 11.73% vs 12.87%) and PAT INR58.08 crore (up 75%). The order book reached INR1,304 crore (up 159%), 64% power transmission solutions and 36% new and renewable energy. Management guided to 40%-plus revenue growth in FY27 and a dividend of INR2 per share was recommended. Standalone figures were also read out, with FY26 standalone revenue of INR448 crore and PAT of INR46 crore.

BESS EPC revenue of INR43 crore (reported as Q4 revenue of INR46 crore) came via group company Advait Green Energy.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40%-plus in FY27, described as conservative by management; it said FY26 growth was about 80%.
FY27 order book targeted at INR1,600-1,650 crore by end of FY27 against an order pipeline of about INR2,000 crore.
Segment mix shifting by about 10 percentage points a year; FY27 targeted at roughly 65:35 (PTS:NRE).
Margin improvement of about 1 percentage point expected in FY27; electrolyser margins 5%-10% initially, rising to about 20% in the subsequent year.
FY27 total capex of INR300-350 crore, including about INR137 crore for PTS/IPP and INR75 crore for BESS and electrolyser subsidiaries; FY26 PTS capex about INR100 crore funded internally.

demand_pricing: Order execution timelines are typically 6 to 18 months depending on business type.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and margin expectations?

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on commodity cost inflation to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding will use both equity and debt in a mix based on business composition, and equity dilution would happen only if it benefits shareholders. No quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of ~10% in FY26 is the lowest in 5 years: how much is deliberate discretionary cost management versus sustainable savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram Charan said the cost actions are structural and automation-led, not a one-off squeeze. Headcount rose ~100-120 people YoY, with ReArch hiring offset by a ~70 reduction in core MF operations. Total cost growth was 9% including depreciation and 7.8% excluding it, with QoQ cost growth under 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Passive mix shift typically hurts RTA yields more than AMC yields. Is there scope to renegotiate RTA pricing on passives or to gain bargaining power on the active book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said passives are under 10% of AUM and already priced at very low levels, so there is no room to renegotiate. Yield compression QoQ (<1%) came from mix, not from lower rates in any asset class. Ram Charan said the mix shift is an argument to raise with AMCs, but it is not a decisive one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-5 bps AMC fee cut be passed to RTA fees? Is any RTA fee negotiation under way?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete RTA fee change has been agreed. Discussions may happen, but management said it is comfortable with the price-value equation and does not expect a material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Should yield decline be modelled at the historical 3-3.5% for FY27 and FY28, given that margins have previously dropped from 46-47% to 42-44%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5% is the 5-year average and should be used as a conservative model input, with the aim being a lower number, possibly under 3%. On margins, Anuj Kumar said 46% was reached about 5 quarters ago, dropped to 42%, and has now been regained over 4 quarters. He attributed the earlier fall to investments in non-revenue businesses made over 2022-2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for employee cost, overall expenses and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth is guided below 5% and total expense growth below 9%, with increments effective from Q2 FY27. No formal margin guidance was given; the aim is to retain the Q4 FY26 margin of ~46.5% after salary increases, investments and yield compression.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~20% non-MF growth be built in FY27 with KRA flat, and what is the breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a base of ~INR60-62 crore quarterly non-MF revenue, or ~INR250 crore annualised. It needs ~INR45-50 crore of increment: payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore (quoted as INR4-5 crore in one place and ~INR15 crore in another), with ConsenPro and GIFT City adding a few crore.

qa_highlights.question: KRA: what is the price cut, and how is FY27 revenue flat after it?
qa_highlights.answer: The industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 is expected to reduce KRA revenue by ~INR8 crore on a base of ~INR42-43 crore. NSE KRA integration adds ~INR3 crore, leaving a ~INR5 crore gap that management expects to close through new-logo growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: ConsenPro is a commercial DPDP-compliance product built inside Think360 from an internal captive offering. It covers consent management, data discovery, regulatory reporting and consulting. Management expects ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies to need it over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Could a single KYC regime through CKYC reduce KRA pricing or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CKYC is not yet eligible to substitute for KRA KYC. KRA runs a second verification layer (name match, face match, DOB and address against DigiLocker or UIDAI), so the risk is seen as a watch item rather than an immediate threat.

KRA: a ~INR8 crore fee cut from 1 April 2026 is only partly offset by ~INR3 crore from NSE KRA. FY27 flat guidance depends on new-logo growth to fill a ~INR5 crore gap. A possible single-KYC/CKYC shift is a watch item.

ReArch execution: a 5-year programme with ~2 years done and ~3-4% behind the schedule curve. The data lake is due in 1H FY27, and the data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform are due within 3-4 months. Non-MF margin target is 20% by end FY27.

Non-MF growth dependence: ~20% FY27 growth needs ~INR45-50 crore of incremental revenue. The breakdown includes ~INR20 crore from payments, with a new-logo pipeline (SIFs, ConsenPro, GIFT City) still early.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-asset MF revenue decline YoY despite transaction growth?
