rows.why: Credit disbursals fell QoQ for three quarters (₹710 crore, ₹610 crore, ₹530 crore) and management gave no quantified recovery target, though credit distribution is up 130% YoY to ₹5.3 billion.

rows.label: No further cash realization increase
rows.why: Cash realization per order rose on mix and the November pricing change, but management said it would not bake in further increases.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term penetration, margin discipline and the LAS and wealth build-out, but evasive on July volumes, credit disbursal declines and wealth/AMC specifics; analysts pushed on disbursal softness, IPL-driven acquisition cost and the restricted-basket policy.

543235|2026-09.headline: Angel One Q2 FY27: consolidated PAT up 58.2% YoY to ₹3.35 bn on revenue of ₹14.3 bn (+18.9%); standalone OPM 48.9%.
543235|2026-09.overview: Revenue held broadly flat sequentially despite softer trading after regulatory changes, while profit grew much faster on operating leverage and a larger client funding book. Consolidated operating margin rose to 45.1% from 34.5% a year ago; normalised for IPL spend and ESOP reversals it was 43.8% versus 43.6% in Q1. Management kept the standalone broking-plus-distribution margin guidance at about 45% annually and reported record average funding book (₹74.5 bn) and record credit distribution in September (annualised run rate ₹33 bn). Client additions were about 1.5 mn, up 11.6% QoQ. Management said October F&O industry ADTO was up about 39% month-to-date versus September (as of 14 October) and linked near-term upside to the SEBI closing auction session (CAS) circular.

financial_highlights.change: +58% YoY (58.2% as stated in opening remarks)
vs 34.5% a year ago (>1,000 bps); 43.8% normalised vs 43.6% QoQ

segments.name: Broking (direct/assisted)
segments.commentary: Gross broking share fell to ~55% of revenue from ~60% a year ago. Net broking income split is ~75% direct and ~25% AP channel. September average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 mn, up ~12% from August.

segments.name: Market share
segments.commentary: Retail F&O turnover share 22.1% for the quarter, rising to 22.5% in September; cash share moderated. Options premium turnover share 19.7%. Commodities turnover more than doubled YoY with share down to 44% as the market expanded.

segments.name: Lending (MTF/funding)
segments.commentary: Interest income ₹5.1 bn. About 84% of funded clients have exposure below ₹100,000; 82% of closing book is under 30 days old. Lending rate held at 14.99% despite higher RBI-linked borrowing costs. Management said delinquencies remain negligible.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution income ~₹71 crore in the quarter, about 5% of revenue, helped by credit distribution and IPO activity. Management does not disclose the split. Regular plans are about one-third of MF distribution.

segments.name: Wealth (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹160 bn, up 19.1% QoQ. Management said margins will be in line with industry (ultra-HNI industry yields near 0.5%) and that the book is focused on annuity-based assets. Some AUM is in custody and does not earn fees; management called this a very small number.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹6 bn. Management is evaluating a comprehensive play and plans to bring in a new leader; no timeline given.

segments.name: New businesses (drag)
segments.commentary: Cash burn from new businesses at about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, up from 2.5%-3% about six quarters ago.

guidance_outlook: Standalone broking-plus-distribution operating margin guided at about 45% on an annual basis; quarterly variation expected. Management said 40-45% is comfortable and it may go towards 50% at times.
Consolidated operating margin guided at 40-45% in the near term; management expects improvement as other businesses contribute meaningfully over the next 2-3 years.
Employee cost guided at about ₹1,100 crore for FY27 including ESOP cost, flat YoY; employee count about 3,050 as of 30 September with backfills slowed.
Brand (IPL) spend expected to decline as a percentage of revenue over time.

Upgraded probability of default model used for credit distribution.
US stocks piloted via IFSC GAP licence (GIFT City) with a US brokerage partner; live pilot with a set of customers and orders flowing.
Cybersecurity stack strengthened with AI-driven vulnerability detection and automated remediation.

Client additions of about 1.5 mn in Q2, up 11.6% QoQ; management says activation trends have improved and NSE active share rose each month of the quarter.
SIP registrations up nearly 12% QoQ; management declined to read much into the September decline.
Management sees F&O pricing as right and is not planning to change it; price elasticity exists but trust is a key driver.
Net broking realisation rose partly on commodities mix; per-segment realisations not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 45% margin guidance include IPL spend and how is employee cost so low?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the ~45% annual guidance for broking plus distribution includes all expenses including IPL. Employee cost fell due to attrition and one-time costs in Q1; FY27 employee cost guided at ~₹1,100 crore, flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross client acquisition slower than the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said acquisitions were up 11% vs Q1 and the company is focused on activation and marginal CAC across channels, including AP, performance marketing and organic. Management said it would invest where growth is available at the right price.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP registrations drop in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said SIP registration numbers vary month-to-month and can be optical (counting edits); a broader period gives a better read, and management tracks SIP inflows and active SIPs.

qa_highlights.question: How is rising borrowing cost affecting MTF and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said lending rate stays at 14.99% with no change planned; borrowing cost rose marginally after the RBI benchmark hike but is within tolerance, with NIMs not materially affected. Bhavin said blue-chip and good stocks make up over 85% of the MTF book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wealth AUM fee yield and how much is earning fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Shobhit said margins will track industry levels (about 0.5% in ultra-HNI) and most of the book is annuity-based. Amit said assets were acquired through the year, so applying yield to closing AUM overstates revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drag from new businesses on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the cash burn from new businesses is about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, versus about 2.5%-3% six quarters ago when scale was low.

qa_highlights.question: Will the closing auction session circular help F&O volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said the circular provides clarity and is a tailwind for near-term F&O, and that pricing is working and not under review.

risks_watch: Regulatory changes (F&O and CAS) are reducing market volumes; management expects a gradual recovery but timing is uncertain.
Cash segment share fell while MTF grew; management attributes this to segment mix, but it is worth tracking.
Competition from new corporate-backed brokerages with lower pricing; management says trust and brand support pricing.
Net active clients have fallen over two years even as total users rose (questioned by Mohit Surana); activation trend is the key metric to watch.
IPL and brand spend, plus AP channel and new business cash burn of 3.5%-4%, weigh on margins.
Insurance commission reset (IRDAI consultation) and US stock pilot are early-stage and not yet material.

543238|2026-03.headline: UTI AMC FY26 standalone normalized PAT fell to Rs 643 crore from Rs 653 crore, while core PAT rose to Rs 460 crore from Rs 447 crore.
543238|2026-03.overview: UTI AMC reported FY26 standalone core income of Rs 1,255 crore (up from Rs 1,180 crore) and normalized core PAT of Rs 460 crore (up from Rs 447 crore). Consolidated normalized PAT fell to Rs 511 crore from Rs 731 crore, and consolidated normalized core PAT fell to Rs 452 crore from Rs 492 crore. Costs rose sharply: consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was up about 14% YoY even after a one-time VRS and family pension charge of about Rs 130 crore taken in Q3. The company declared a Rs 40 per share FY26 dividend and management said it sees the payout trend at about 95% of profits. Management's single stated priority is growth in MF AUM, with cost discipline as the second.

segments.commentary: AUM Rs 5,280 crore across five active funds. SDOF-II fully exited with 13.4% IRR; SDOF-IV launched in Q2 with Rs 674 crore AUM against a Rs 1,500 crore plus Rs 500 crore greenshoe target.

Standalone other administrative expenses guided to rise about 7-8% (around 8% cited); consolidated 100-200 bps higher, around 10%, due to UTI Pension Fund geographic expansion.

Weighted average yield expected to dilute by about 1-2 bps in FY27 from a mix shift toward ETFs, index funds and low-duration debt funds. Current yield breakup: equity and hybrid 75 bps, ETF and index about 8 bps, cash and arbitrage about 10 bps, income funds 18-19 bps, blended about 32 bps.
Passive pipeline: filings planned for UTI NIFTY 500 Index Fund, UTI BSE Index Sector Leaders, UTI NIFTY India New Age Consumption and UTI NIFTY India Internet Fund, each in index and ETF form.

Cloud infrastructure upgrade added about Rs 8 crore to other expenses in FY26.

Net equity flows were close to zero in FY26 after negative flows in the prior two years; 8 of 19 core funds recorded positive net sales.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off in Q4/FY26 expenses, and how should employee and other expenses be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 130 crore of VRS and family pension one-off was provided in Q3 FY26, plus about Rs 4 crore for the Labour Code. Analyst noted consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was still up 14% YoY; management attributed this to variable pay and recruitment across three businesses. FY27 guidance: standalone employee cost Rs 90-95 crore per quarter, consolidated Rs 125-130 crore; other admin expenses +7-8% standalone and about 10% consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How did customer acquisition go during the March volatility, and what schemes attract first-time SIP investors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no sharp pick-up in new investors in March; SIP stoppages rose seasonally. February new SIP additions were better than the industry. First-time investors mainly choose index funds, often with Rs 1,000-1,500 SIP tickets. New PAN acquisition is now a sales metric, with FY26 target to grow the 7.16 lakh count.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of SEBI's revised norms from 1 April, and what is the yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exit load TER cut by 5 bps, plus some base TER rationalisation; management expects the impact to pass through to intermediaries and sees no effect on AMC yield. Yield may dilute by 1-2 bps in FY27 due to mix shift to ETFs and low-duration debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to return equity net sales to positive territory?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is raising SIP book. Management is repositioning sales teams to sell multiple funds across value, GARP and quality growth styles, to reduce pro-cyclicality to performance. Net equity flows were close to zero in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the employee count fall while sales staff grows, and is RM headcount rising further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix is being corrected toward revenue-generating roles. It does not expect RM count to rise much further from about 260 UFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and SIF launches?
qa_highlights.answer: International AUM is under pressure from foreign outflows and currency weakness; management plans to hold ground and bring institutional clients into alternatives. SIF: at least one fund targeted this year, first product unlikely to be priced above plain-vanilla MF yields; higher yield depends on long-short differentiation.

qa_highlights.question: How should the Rs 4,000-4,500 crore cash and investments be deployed, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no plans for cash build-up or buybacks; cash retained for liquidity and possible M&A. Dividend trend line is roughly 95% payout including Rs 40 per share for FY26. Business described as not capital-intensive.

543238|2026-06.headline: UTI AMC Q1 FY27 standalone core revenue flat YoY at Rs 308 crore, core PAT up 1% YoY to Rs 119 crore; dividend payout held above 95%.

segments.name: UTI Pension Fund (100% subsidiary)

segments.name: UTI International

543245|2026-09.headline: Gland Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR 18,336 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 27% and PAT up 58%.
543245|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR 18,336 million (+23% YoY), led by CDMO (+31% to INR 8,227 million) and US sales (+42% to INR 11,795 million). Reported EBITDA rose 53% to INR 4,804 million (26% margin), and adjusted EBITDA was INR 5,030 million (27%) after INR 226 million non-cash ESOP cost. PAT grew 58% to INR 2,908 million, with ROW revenue weak on delayed NUPCO tender results and Cenexi posting an EBITDA loss of EUR 6 million from its annual shutdown. Management kept full-year guidance at 15% constant-currency growth and announced a further INR 3,000 crore capacity programme.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 8,227 million (+31% YoY), about 45% of revenue; H1 INR 17,142 million (+25%), about 47% of revenue. Growth from commercial supply of earlier contracts, new launches and new development/manufacturing partnerships.

segments.name: Critical injectables
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 10,109 million (+18% YoY); H1 INR 19,197 million (+18%). Driven by existing portfolio, recent launches, new customers and higher volumes.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 11,795 million (+42% YoY); H1 INR 21,605 million (+37%). Four US launches in the quarter; management says growth excluding Cenexi is about the same as reported.

segments.name: Europe and other regulated markets
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 4,110 million (+23% YoY); H1 INR 8,598 million (+17%).

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 2,044 million, held back by market-specific supply and tender issues, notably the delayed NUPCO (Saudi Arabia) tender results. India revenue was INR 387 million.

segments.name: Cenexi
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue EUR 41 million (vs EUR 40 million a year earlier) with EBITDA of about minus EUR 6 million, due to planned annual summer shutdowns. Management expects profitability from Q3 and is prioritising margin over top-line growth.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance unchanged at 15% on a constant-currency basis; management said currency impact is hard to predict.
US growth expected to sustain in H2, with no lumpiness, driven by new launches and CDMO business; ROW expected to improve once NUPCO tender results are announced.
Cenexi guidance from Q1 (about EUR 200 million revenue at high-single-digit margin for FY27) is still in place, per CFO, with the lower Q2 number already in the estimate.
Launch contribution from new products expected to add about 6-7% to growth; new US launches include methylprednisolone suspension (generic Medrol), with GLP-1 CDMO launches possible in Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Cenexi expected to restore profitability from Q3 FY27, which should normalise the effective tax rate.
R&D spend to rise slightly over time, while management aims to keep margins intact.
capex_capacity: INR 2,000 crore programme (previously announced) for ophthalmic capacity, a new BFS line, and oncology/sterile capacity with isolator technology; additional bag manufacturing capacity awaiting US FDA inspection.
New brownfield project at Pashamylaram: about INR 1,000 crore for three isolator-based vial lines, approved in the call, with commercial operations from FY2030.
Greenfield project at Vizag SEZ: land acquired, project plan in progress, capex not yet quantified; Board approval expected next quarter, programme about four years.

Management said total capex of about INR 5,000 crore over four years including greenfield, with about INR 3,000 crore excluding it, adding about 300-400 million units of capacity. Current capacity is about 1.7 billion units.
Liquid vial utilisation at 92%, expected near 102% next year; some lines are fully occupied and planned shutdowns are being deferred for lack of capacity.
Cenexi: new vial and lyophilisation block at BLA and high-speed ampoule line at Fontenay on track.
demand_pricing: Management said CDMO is growing faster than the regular business and will keep outgrowing it; the pipeline has grown in quality and scale.
Microsphere and respiratory CDMO contracts are at early tech-transfer stage (three projects signed), with royalty-based revenue expected from FY2029-30.
Management said CDMO margins are about 5-10% better than critical injectables, since the mix is more regulated-market weighted and includes Cenexi.
Saudi NUPCO tender: about 13 products bid, several won; the timing of the tender announcement remains uncertain.
Pricing and competitive commentary was limited; demand described as robust across ophthalmic, bags and liquid vials.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year outlook for US and ROW revenue, and is US growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year guidance stays at 15% constant-currency growth. US growth is driven by launches and CDMO, with no lumpiness, and ROW is expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capex and capacity addition over the next four years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed about INR 5,000 crore including greenfield. Excluding greenfield, about INR 3,000 crore would add 300-400 million units.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex backed by take-or-pay contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some contracts are take-or-pay and some are not, but most are transfers from commercialised sites with forecasts in place. The policy was to add lines at about 20% idle capacity, and current utilisation is above that.

qa_highlights.question: Will Cenexi's FY27 guidance of EUR 200 million revenue and high-single-digit margin still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the lower Q2 number was already planned, and the earlier guidance is still in place, to be updated if changed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China in-licensing (CIO and BD hires) aimed at India or global markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on innovative products for India, plus global biologics acquisitions. The second in-licensed long-acting injectable is a $2 billion product under patent, with a three-year timeline; Gland will run clinicals and act as commercial partner, and manufacturing stays in China. The first, at $800 million, will be transferred to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO versus critical injectables split and margin difference?
qa_highlights.answer: CDMO covers third-party-owned IP and co-development, while critical injectables covers Gland-owned ANDAs and in-licensed products. Management said CDMO margins are 5-10% higher, and Cenexi is included in CDMO.

risks_watch: Cenexi: Q2 EBITDA loss of EUR 6 million; the company must deliver about EUR 111 million revenue in H2 at an 18-20% margin to meet the FY27 guidance, per an analyst's arithmetic.
Capacity constraints: vial lines are near full utilisation and planned shutdowns are being deferred; a lag before the brownfield lines come online (FY2030) could cost growth.
Rest-of-world exposure, especially Saudi NUPCO tender timing, which is still pending.
FX: constant-currency growth is not disclosed for Q2 or H1, and about 80% of revenue is exports.
Cost of new US biologics acquisition and in-licensing pipeline; R&D intensity is set to rise.
Dundigal US FDA inspection concluded with four procedural observations (not data integrity or repeat); the bag line awaits FDA inspection before commercialisation.
Greenfield Vizag capex not yet quantified and Board approval pending next quarter.
Leadership transition: new CEO Deepak Sapra joins 16 November 2026; new Cenexi President Ajay Sahni joined this week.

Cautious on Cenexi, where the message is margin repair over top-line growth. 543248|2026-03.headline: RBA India Q4 FY26 SSSG hit 6.3%, the highest in 12 quarters, while Indonesia took a INR120 crore impairment and the company is being acquired by Inspira Global.
543248|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 SSSG of 6.3%, up from 4.5% in the prior quarter, with full-year SSSG at 4%. Full-year revenue was INR2,271 crore, restaurant EBITDA margin 11.6% and company EBITDA margin 5.8%. Gross margin exited Q4 at 70.2%, ahead of the FY29 target. Indonesia drew a INR120 crore impairment on a DCF valuation, with Popeyes (24 outlets) losing IDR25 billion, and the company is set to be acquired by Inspira Global, with revised outlook promised after the deal closes in Q1.

segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG 6.3%, FY26 SSSG 4%; net 68 stores opened in FY26, within 60-80 annual guidance. Restaurant EBITDA 11.6%, company EBITDA 5.8%. Dine-in traffic up 18% over three years; 91% of orders digital.

segments.name: Indonesia (Burger King)
segments.commentary: Store-level EBITDA positive IDR8 billion for FY26 and positive in Q4; dine-in ADS month-on-month above prior year except one September blip. Delivery ADS cut in Q4 for margin repair, now back to 6.2-6.4 range per management.

segments.name: Indonesia (Popeyes)
segments.commentary: 25 restaurants reduced to 24 after one closure; management described the business as struggling and said it should move to another owner's portfolio. FY26 loss IDR25 billion.

segments.name: Café / beverages
segments.commentary: BK Café now in all restaurants except a few with location limits. Management has not put marketing money behind Café except a 4-week window last year; long-term ADS goal of INR25,000 per restaurant per day over 4-5 years. Current new Café restaurants run below average.

guidance_outlook: Free cash flow neutral for India business targeted in 4-6 quarters (Sumit); analyst read this as FY28 FCF-positive, management confirmed the target.
Revised company outlook to be given in Q1 FY27 once the Inspira Global acquisition closes.
Annual net restaurant openings of 60-80 to continue.
Electric broiler (uses about half the utilities) to be installed in all India restaurants within about two months; solar rollout continues.
Indonesia BK restaurant-level EBITDA expected to cover its G&A about four quarters away, or in the year after the current one (Varman); no timeline given for Popeyes.
Management did not give new gross margin targets beyond 70%; will return at an appropriate time.

Electric broiler rollout across India restaurants nearing completion; one more round of installs pending.
Electric fryer portfolio being expanded for vegetarian items; LPG-to-PNG conversions under way where PNG is available.
Indonesia long-term strategy plan being prepared; funding requirement to be disclosed later, no figure given.
demand_pricing: Value anchored on 2for79 and 2for99 price points; coupon/app deals and shareable meal bundles also drive dine-in traffic.
Premium layer (King's Collection, Whopper Deluxe range, Korean LTO, Kimchi ad) lifting APC; management did not share Deluxe product mix or SSSG contribution.
Gross margin gains credited to cluster-led supply chain, delivery product-mix and discount changes, and high-margin add-ons (fizz drinks, Waffle Cone).
Delivery profitability improved by 2% by lowering discounts and changing product mix; management did not quantify the margin improvement further.
Management said there is no current danger to India operations from the LNG/LPG supply disruption; no restaurants closed for a day, but LPG-dependent outlets faced challenges.

qa_highlights.question: How has Café ADS performed in mature stores, and what is the incremental ADS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose Café split. Early-converted cohorts sit well above average. Target is around INR25,000 per restaurant per day over 4-5 years. Newer Café stores have lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the cash burn (about INR350 crore used in operations, cash down from about INR500 crore to about INR150 crore) and the outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sumit said cash is about INR190 crore as of March, cash from operations rose from INR99 crore to INR132 crore, and India is targeting FCF neutrality in 4-6 quarters. Q4 generated INR40 crore. Analyst confirmed FY28 FCF-positive target; management agreed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR120 crore impairment booked, is this a full exit, what is the new promoter's plan, and what is the Indonesia breakeven timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment came from a DCF on consolidated Indonesia business; management called it a one-time provision fully covering the balance-sheet requirement. Varman declined to give a timeline or exit decision until the new promoter aligns. Sumit said the BK side needs about four more quarters to cover its own G&A.

qa_highlights.question: Will Lenexis (promoter's Chinese wok brand) be merged or licensed with RBA, and what protects minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Varman said the businesses are separate, no discussions have taken place, and the focus is on Indonesia structural changes. Deal awaits government approvals with no timing given.

qa_highlights.question: Is CCI approval the only pending item for the open offer, and how is LNG supply disruption being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that CCI approval is pending. On LNG, the new broiler is electric, about half the utilities; electric fryers are being added; LPG restaurants converted to PNG where possible. No percentage split given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin expansion comes from product mix versus sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Varman said it is a combined effort: cluster-based supplier proximity lowers transport and input cost, and premium items and add-ons (fizz drinks, Waffle Cone) carry high margins. No split quantified.

risks_watch: Indonesia: INR120 crore impairment; further funding need and further write-downs not quantified; Popeyes (24 outlets) has no disposal timeline.
Pending CCI approval and government approvals for the Inspira Global / new promoter deal; revised guidance deferred until Q1 FY27.
Related-party exposure: the new promoter also runs Lenexis Foodworks (Chinese wok brand); management said no merger or licensing discussions are under way.

543248|2026-06.headline: India SSSG hit 12.6% in Q1 FY27 with revenue up 23.6% to INR682 crore and restaurant EBITDA of INR90 crore (13.2% margin).

India gross margin rose to 70.8% and company EBITDA more than doubled to INR52.7 crore. Indonesia remained loss-making at the Popeyes level but Burger King Indonesia reached positive restaurant EBITDA, with consolidated restaurant EBITDA of INR3.3 crore. A new promoter group has closed its stake acquisition, and management is working on a capital allocation plan for the next 3 to 5 years, with no details yet.

segments.commentary: 590 restaurants (+71 YoY, +9 QoQ), 83% of group revenue; SSSG 12.6%, ADS INR1,31,000, gross margin 70.8%, restaurant EBITDA INR90 crore. Management targets around 80 net additions a year.

segments.commentary: 137 restaurants (down from 179 after closing non-profitable units, per management), 15% of group revenue; ADS INR1,02,000, revenue INR124 crore, restaurant EBITDA INR6.4 crore. 543252|2026-09.headline: Fairchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 49.7% YoY to Rs 167 crore at a 10.5% EBITDA margin, helped by lower raw material costs after the crude soybean oil duty cut.
543252|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 167 crore (up 49.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 10.5% and net profit of Rs 10.2 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 343 crore (up 41.4%), EBITDA Rs 35.4 crore at a 10.3% margin, and net profit Rs 21.2 crore. Management attributed gains to better price realisation from lower raw material costs, higher finished product prices, and lower dimer acid imports. Plant utilisation is still low at about 60-65%, and management expects it to improve as raw material availability rises after the crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%.

segments.name: Capacity and utilisation
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 60-65% (CFO: close to 65%). Management targets 5% improvement every quarter but gave no timeline for reaching 85-90%. Management says it has not lost market share.

segments.name: New fatty-acid product
segments.commentary: Small-capacity plant using novel technology, import-substituting with export potential; commissioning has slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec quarter (after Diwali), with start-up hiccups expected. Management said the market is very large if the process succeeds, and a PFAD bypass product from palm oil is already commercialised and is a different product.

segments.commentary: Realisation Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26. Exports to the US are on hold due to high freight costs. Value-added products (linoleic acid, distilled dimer) are expected to earn a 5-10% realisation premium. Chinese dumping has fallen, mainly due to lower Chinese export incentives, with rupee depreciation also helping.

segments.commentary: Cosmetics business is expected to be hit in the near term by slowing European demand and high US import duties. Approval cycle took 2.5 years. Management expects long-term recovery since only four players globally make the product, and sees UK as the sole Cargill plant location.

segments.commentary: Working capital cycle guided at 90-100 days for domestic sales, longer for exports, around 100 days overall; trade receivables about Rs 100 crore. No near-term expansion plans; capex only if the new product succeeds; land of Rs 12 crore bought from promoter, already in use for operations and workers' colony.

543253|2026-03.headline: Mrs. Bectors FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore (+9.1%) but EBITDA grew only 2.5% to INR257.7 crore, with margin at 12.6%.
543253|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 8.9% YoY to INR485.86 crore, with Biscuits up 8.4% and Bakery up 8.5%, and Bakery EBITDA margin at 12.7% (+25 bps). FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,043.6 crore (+9.1%), EBITDA INR257.7 crore (+2.5%, margin 12.6%) and PAT INR140.9 crore (6.9% margin). Management flagged a new cost shock from the West Asia conflict (about 3% cost impact on packaging, palm oil, crude-linked items, labour and logistics), which it says is covered by price increases and Project IMPACT savings. Export incentive (DFIA) remains on hold, and exports stayed in low-single-digit growth in Q4.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.4% YoY and FY26 grew 6.7%; management targets low-to-mid-teens growth in FY27. About 65% of biscuit sales come from INR5 and INR10 packs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Low-single-digit growth in Q4 and single-digit for FY26, hit by US tariffs (peak 50%) and the West Asia conflict. FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens growth; the Bahrain and Kuwait GCC markets are affected.

US tariffs were cut from their 50% peak, and new US retailer projects have started onboarding. Export incentive (DFIA) restart is still pending with the government.

qa_highlights.answer: Navratri moved into March (from April last year), which hit bread demand in North India. Management called it seasonal and said English Oven is still growing at high-teens.

543253|2026-09.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.3% YoY to INR 630.5 crore, with EBITDA margin held at 13.1% despite steeper input inflation.
543253|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR 630.5 crore, up 14.3% YoY and 14.9% QoQ, with EBITDA up 19.1% to INR 82.5 crore. EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps YoY to 13.1% and was flat QoQ, while gross margin fell from about 47.2% in Q1 to about 46% on RM and packaging inflation. Domestic biscuits grew low teens, bakery (English Oven, NaturBaked, Cremica bakery) grew high teens, and exports grew more slowly on Middle East disruption and freight. Management expects margins to stay under pressure in Q3 and to recover toward 13.5-14% in Q4.

segments.name: Exports (biscuits)
segments.commentary: Growth slowed in Q2 due to Middle East disruption, freight spikes and delayed container pickups. Management still guides to mid-teens export growth for FY27.

segments.commentary: Grew mid-to-high teens in both volume and value in Q2, with QSR recovery cited. Ongoing B2B store expansion by partners.

Export shipping and freight costs were severely affected by the West Asia conflict; Middle East business was hit, though freight is showing early easing signs.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition in north and central India biscuits, given large players and regional players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intensity is high from large and regional players; the company is responding through distribution expansion, 10-15% more distributors, and quick commerce premium launches (shortbread with 25% butter, Zero Maida coconut biscuit), with three new quick commerce products planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook for revenue and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year revenue growth expected to end at mid-teens. Q3 margin target is to hold around 13.1%, and Q4 is targeted at 13.5-14%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the bread (bakery) growth and how did institutional and retail split?
qa_highlights.answer: English Oven volume grew mid-teens and value very high-teens; institutional bakery grew mid-to-high teens in both volume and value. English Oven CAGR has been high-teens for five years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports slow in Q2, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East exposure, freight spikes and delayed container pickups slowed orders. Relationships are intact and the full-year export outlook is still mid-teens.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase was taken in Q2 and expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 3% in Q2 over Q1; full-year around 5-6%. Further increases in October and partly November.

qa_highlights.answer: Both raw material and packaging inflation. Price recovery was about 1% short, which accounts for the roughly 1% gap in gross margin. Gross margin is expected to hold at current levels in Q3 and Q4.

rows.why: Q4 PAT was flat QoQ at ~INR1,684 crore (down ~INR100 crore per analyst), new provisioning on CPSE/state lending is a drag, and management says market rates are rising, which could compress margins on bids where IRFC wins over 60%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Metro railway and state-government funding products are to be launched soon, with cost-plus and full-risk bid models both planned, but no dates or sizes were given.

rows.label: Diversification to non-railway and state/metro lending
rows.why: Non-railway is about 5% of AUM after ~INR35,000 crore FY26 disbursements at 100-120 bps vs 35-40 bps on railways, with a 30-40% non-railway aspiration near term and metro/state talks to launch soon.

rows.label: NTPC/UP JV tender and DFC corridor pipeline
rows.why: Pipeline built from zero at start of FY26 to ~INR74,000 crore sanctions; NTPC/UP JV tender of INR28,000-29,000 crore could give IRFC up to INR16,000-17,000 crore, but awards are not yet made.

rows.label: Borrowing cost below G-Sec and ECB mix 30-35%
rows.why: Management targets borrowing cost below G-Sec yield and an ECB share of 30-35%, with yen ECBs of $300M and $400M done and a $1.1 billion yen bid open, though domestic rates are rising.

tone.note: Management was confident on sanction and disbursement growth, the NIM path to 1.65% and zero-NPA lending, but evasive on ROA and tax-adjusted economics; analysts pushed on Q4 PAT decline, provisioning and the feasibility of the 60:40 mix.

543257|2026-06.headline: IRFC Q1 FY27: disbursement slow at about INR2,000 crore and AUM dipped QoQ, but management reiterates about INR5 lakh crore year-end AUM.
543257|2026-06.overview: Management framed FY27 as a consolidation year, building toward 2030 midterm and 2037 long-term plans after FY26 agreements above INR75,000 crore and disbursements above INR35,000 crore. Q1 disbursement was about INR2,000 crore and AUM declined slightly on an accrual basis, which management attributed to scheduled repayments from railways that fall in September. Management said the company is now a near-record on revenue and PAT, helped by a forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements. The call focused on the "Fund in India" conduit model, high-speed rail and DFC pipeline, NIM targets, and questions on fertiliser exposure and the agreement-to-disbursement lag.

segments.name: Railways (core, sole financier)
segments.commentary: Management says IRFC remains the sole financing arm for Indian Railways; no railway business was booked in FY24 but FY26 saw a restart in diversification. Railway repayments drive quarterly AUM dips.

segments.name: Diversified / non-railway (fertiliser, metro, GenCo, ports)
segments.commentary: Three HURL urea plants (Gorakhpur, Barauni, Sindri) are financed on railway-linkage grounds, refinanced from SBI-led lenders at 50bps+ lower cost. Hyderabad Metro Phase 1 refinancing signed; Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) pending decision.

guidance_outlook: Year-end FY27 AUM targeted around INR5 lakh crore (management: possibly INR4.95 lakh crore); mid-year guidance of about INR5 lakh crore also referenced.
FY27 disbursement guided to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore; Q2-Q4 expected to pick up, with some refinancing assets in the pipeline.
NIM target: about 10bps average annual improvement, 2% by end-2030; FY27 NIM targeted above 1.6%, with Q4 NIM expected to be higher than the 1.65% full-year ambition referenced by the analyst.

Planning around INR50,000-plus crore disbursement per year for the next decade; high-speed rail and DFC pipeline cited as more than INR50,000-60,000 crore per year, with metro and rapid rail adding INR20,000-30,000 crore per year.
Targets new lending at about 8% with spread above 100bps; repayments on legacy assets at 35-40bps lower margin.
capex_capacity: Planned high-speed rail corridors (7 announced) with financing need about INR16 lakh crore; DFC about INR3 lakh crore; combined about INR20 lakh crore, per management.
Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore; Phase 1 refinancing already signed.
Greenfield projects take 3 to 5 years from agreement to first funding, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says recent open-tender rates for GenCo and transport projects are around 8%, and IRFC is comfortable lending at that level with 100bps+ margin.
Fund in India: IRFC intends to act as a conduit for bilateral and multilateral funding, offering bespoke tenor and currency solutions.
Competitors' NIMs are falling across the sector per management; IRFC's low overhead cost is cited as the advantage.
Q1 disbursement was small because the pipeline is thin; management says it is not reliant on FY26 agreements converting in-year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hold the INR5 lakh crore AUM guidance at half-year and end FY27, and what is the disbursement and AUM growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about INR5 lakh crore AUM by year-end, noting it may land at INR4.95 lakh crore. FY27 disbursement is expected to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore. The Q1 AUM dip reflects a September repayment from railways.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 2% YoY against AUM growth of about 4%, implying NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM rose from 1.40% in FY25 to 1.50% in FY26 and is expected to exceed 1.6% by year-end. Legacy 35-40bps assets are repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets, which is a gradual effect over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the material other income in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements, reflecting rupee appreciation against the yen. Management said the gain is accounted per Ind AS and a corresponding metro receipt is expected in Q2. Last year's Q4 saw a INR7 crore forex loss.

qa_highlights.question: How are the fertiliser borrowers linked to railways, and is there sponsor support or guarantee for these loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HURL urea plants depend on railway sidings for raw material and finished urea movement. Output is sold to government agencies on a cost-plus model with 10-12% margin. Management described the loans as refinancing of an existing SBI-led bank facility, with rate cuts of at least 50bps. No explicit sponsor guarantee was described.

qa_highlights.question: What does the agreements-executed versus disbursement table mean, and why is there a lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR92,799 crore of agreements were largely greenfield, of which about INR37,000 crore has been disbursed. Greenfield funding typically starts 3 to 5 years after agreement, with the remainder expected over 1 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on diversification into metro and infrastructure, and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hyderabad Metro is on track, with Phase 1 refinancing signed and Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) awaiting a decision. Pipeline spans high-speed rail, DFC, metro, rapid rail, ports, GenCo, transco and renewables linked to railways.

risks_watch: Q1 disbursement of about INR2,000 crore leaves the INR35,000 crore-plus FY27 target dependent on a steep ramp in Q2-Q4.
AUM guidance hinges on repayments from railways and new refinancing deals; a September repayment could again lower the AUM figure.
NIM guidance (1.6%+ this year, 2% by 2030) relies on legacy assets at 35-40bps repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets; the call did not provide a quarterly path.
Fertiliser exposure to sister-company-linked borrowers; management cited cost-plus economics but no formal guarantee was described.
Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 decision and the high-speed rail and DFC funding framework remain unconfirmed; the large INR20 lakh crore opportunity is not yet contracted.
Forex gains on yen funding may not recur; the Q1 other income is currency-driven.
543257|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term vision (2030 and 2037), but evasive on specific FY27 numbers, repeatedly saying guidance is "intact" without fixed figures. Management was defensive when questioned on NIM compression and on fertiliser borrower linkages.
key_quotes: We are very comfortable at 8%. Others were never lending at 8%.
We will reach 2% NIM by the end of 2030. That is the target for the company.

rows.why: About INR37,000 crore of the INR92,799 crore agreed has been disbursed, leaving about INR55,000-56,000 crore to disburse, though greenfield funding starts 3 to 5 years after agreement.

rows.why: Legacy assets at 35-40bps lower margin are repaying and being replaced with new lending at about 8% with spread above 100bps, which is the mechanism behind the NIM rise.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 2030 and 2037 vision, the NIM path and the INR5 lakh crore AUM goal, but evasive on FY27 specifics and defensive on NIM compression and fertiliser borrower linkages; analysts pressed on NII growth lagging AUM and on the Q1 other-income forex gain.

543257|2026-09.headline: IRFC reports H1 FY27 revenue up over 20% and PAT up over 10%; management reiterates ~INR5 lakh crore AUM target for FY27.
543257|2026-09.overview: Management said H1 FY27 beat both company guidance and street expectations, with revenue up more than 20% and PAT up more than 10% year on year. The CEO said PAT grew in double digits in five of the last six quarters, the exception being Q4 FY26, which carried provisions for new business under RBI norms. Diversification beyond the Indian Railways single-client model is the core theme, with non-railway lending at margins 2-3.5 times the railway book. The call also covered a large pipeline of railway-linked financing (DFC, high-speed rail, freight JVs) that management expects to start in FY28. Most Q&A was on strategy and shareholder value; the transcript gives no reported Q2 figures beyond the H1 growth rates.

segments.name: Railways (IR) lending
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% plus of AUM is with Railways, at a NIM of about 1.3% (around 35 bps margin on cost-plus). Railway book is being replaced over time by higher-yield non-IR assets.

segments.name: Non-railway lending (diversification)
segments.commentary: Non-IR assets earn margins of 2-3.5 times the railway book, per management; INR35,000 crore of disbursement last year was non-IR. Pipeline covers metros, ports, renewables, thermal power, Gencos linked to Railways, and some road linkages, targeted for Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements to exceed last year's level; guidance reiterated.
AUM target of near INR5 lakh crore (possibly slightly short by INR1,000-2,000 crore) by end FY27; management expects to show progress by Q3.
PAT expected to grow near 10% annually even with flat AUM, as non-IR assets replace railway assets at higher yields.

Railway-related funding of minimum about INR50,000 crore a year from FY28 for next decade, subject to the funding model (multilateral/aggregator role) to be finalised by end FY27; clearer numbers promised in Q3.
Mix target of 60% pure railways and 40% diversification by 2030.
Margin floor of INR0.85-0.90 per the ALM policy on non-railway loans; WACC target of 6.55% to be maintained.
capex_capacity: Management cited a Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat (over 2,000 km, more than INR3 lakh crore), seven sanctioned high-speed rail corridors, and six freight lines planned under JV/PPP; total pie over INR20 lakh crore over about 10 years.
IRFC plans to act as sole financing arm and aggregator, with talks under way with the World Bank, other multilaterals and domestic players; model expected in place by end FY27.
Employee headcount roughly doubled in the last year, per the CEO.
demand_pricing: Floating-rate exposure: repo rate up 25 bps and back-to-back TONAR up 25 bps; management says it passes these through on non-railway loans and that resets are both ways.
Yen borrowing: about USD2 billion raised last year at around 1.8%, now about 2.25% after TONAR increases; hedging cost stated as not above 6.3%.
Term loans from banks are about 25% of the borrowing mix; management claims a 20-30 bps cushion against rate moves.
Prepayment: management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no floor on benchmark-linked pricing, and lowest-in-market cost of funds.
Overhead cost cited at about INR0.15 per unit of lending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities, and what are the main risks on railway capex, asset growth or funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 disbursements will exceed FY26, with non-IR pipeline (metros, ports, renewables, thermal, Gencos, roads) ready for Q3 or early Q4. Railway-linked funding is to start from FY28 at a minimum of INR50,000 crore a year, with the aggregator model to be set by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key financial risks (NIM, borrowing costs, asset quality) in a changing rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO cited a 6.55% WACC, lower than other NBFCs, and a push to raise more 54EC bonds and ECB. Management said the ALM team monitors margins weekly and keeps a minimum spread of INR0.85-0.90 on non-railway loans.

qa_highlights.question: How is non-railway lending priced, and how fast can rate increases be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans are priced on a cost-plus basis, and floating-rate loans reset monthly, quarterly or yearly. Management said a 25 bps repo hike and TONAR increase were passed through, and the company keeps a 20-30 bps cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there prepayment pressure, as seen at other government lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no benchmark floor, and the cheapest funding in the market. Some prepayments by borrowers into IRFC were said to be business wins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM and disbursement vision, and is the INR5 lakh crore AUM target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated near INR5 lakh crore AUM by end FY27 (possibly 1,000-2,000 crore short), up from INR4.85 lakh crore at end FY26. It targets a 60:40 railway-to-diversified mix by 2030 and near-10% PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share price move so much, and what are the dividend and value prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share price moves are outside its control and pointed to fundamentals. It cited an interim dividend of INR1.15 this year against INR1.05 last year, and a payout of about 40% of profit over the last two years.

risks_watch: Funding for the railway-linked pipeline (DFC, high-speed rail, freight lines) depends on a model yet to be finalised with the Ministry, multilaterals and bilaterals; no numbers given yet.
Rising floating rates (repo and TONAR each up 25 bps) and hardening yen hedge costs could squeeze spreads if pass-through lags.
AUM target near INR5 lakh crore may slip by INR1,000-2,000 crore; Q3 is the next checkpoint.
Non-IR loans are ticket-size lumpy (INR10,000-20,000 crore), so disbursement may be concentrated in H2.
Management did not disclose a specific Q2 standalone figure or asset-quality (GNPA/NPA) data in the call.

Management was firm on AUM and disbursement targets but vague on the railway funding model and gave few hard numbers beyond H1 growth rates. It answered the investor-relations question on share price with general market commentary.

numbers are not manufactured; they are earned.

rows.why: Non-IR loans earn 2-3.5 times the railway book, and INR35,000 crore of non-IR disbursement last year, with a 60:40 railway-to-diversified mix targeted by 2030 and the pipeline starting Q3 or early Q4 FY27.

543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

segments.name: Paint categories (Q4 FY26 value growth / volume growth)
segments.commentary: Primers and distemper grew 14.9% value and 9.6% volume; putty and cement paint 12.6% value and 9.5% volume; emulsions 10.5% value and 11.2% volume; enamels and wood coatings 7.2% value and 5.4% volume. All four categories grew in value and volume.

segments.name: Apple Chemie (subsidiary, waterproofing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR27.5 crore (+34.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR75.1 crore (+17.8%). Gross margin around 40% plus/minus 1%. FY27 target is 30%-plus growth.

guidance_outlook: Management is prepared to accept a 2-2.5pp gross margin decline to drive faster top-line growth, while expecting EBITDA margin broadly unchanged.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.
April growth was driven largely by price hikes; some dealer overstocking has occurred, so May-June demand is uncertain.
Industry price increases of about 12% on the overall basket were implemented; management does not foresee another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation deteriorates.
Management expects gross margins across the industry to normalise by Q2 FY27 as raw material costs stabilise, though Q1 may see volatility.
Apple Chemie targets 30%-plus revenue growth in FY27.
No major capex is envisaged until FY29; FCF is expected to step up from FY27 onwards. FY26 dividend proposed at INR5 per share, up 43% from INR3.5.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant, 90,000 KL per annum capacity: final commissioning stage, trial production expected June 2026.
New solvent-based plant and expanded putty plant at Jodhpur have already commenced production in recent months.
Network at 31 March 2026: over 19,350 active dealers, over 12,200 tinting machines, 55 depots across all 28 states.
330 kW solar installation at Kochi factory is fully operational.
demand_pricing: Industry demand recovered from November 2025 after roughly 8 quarters of subdued growth; the Iran war from about March 2026 disrupted raw material supply and pushed some input prices up 50-100%.
The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.
Management said the competitive intensity has moderated over the last couple of quarters; it sees no change in behaviour since JSW's acquisition of Akzo.
Differentiated products make up about 30% of sales and are described as price-inelastic, so margin reduction is expected mainly in the other two-thirds of the portfolio.
Premium emulsions are a growing share; management said value growth has exceeded volume growth in almost all categories over the last 20 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Apple Chemie growth accelerate to 35% in Q4 and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was muted because government contractors' payments were delayed, but Q3 and Q4 grew about 30%-plus; gross margin is about 40% plus/minus 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company pursuing more aggressive market share gains, and will a 200bp gross margin sacrifice be enough to reach about 24% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board judged the company had been too conservative on margins; it will spend more on trade schemes and influencers, lowering gross margin 2-2.5pp while EBITDA margin should hold. Management said yes, 24% growth is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the gross margin reduction come from, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra spend will be netted from revenue through trade discounts and influencer costs, mainly in non-differentiated products. Management said competitive intensity has normalised and the move reflects a wish to grow faster, not a response to competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile double-digit gross growth with single-digit reported growth, and will net sales be sacrificed?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross sales grew double-digit in each of the last five months, but higher trade and influencer discounts cut Q4 net growth to 8.5%. Management does not expect net sales growth to fall back to single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Will more price increases be needed, and how is pricing held if costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation worsens. It said the company now acts independently on pricing and that margins should normalise by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company growing in metros and dealer productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 1 and Tier 2 coverage is now good, and growth will come from deeper dealer throughput, not city size; with about 19,500 dealers it sees room to double sales per dealer.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression of 2-2.5pp from trade and influencer spending; watch whether EBITDA margin holds near 23%.
Gap between gross and net sales growth caused by rising discounts; watch Q1 FY27 net revenue.
Possible overstocking by dealers after April price-led growth; May-June demand is unclear.
Raw material volatility from the Middle East conflict; solvent-based products carry an uncovered cost gap.
Commissioning and ramp-up risk at the Jodhpur water-based plant, targeted for June 2026.
Apple Chemie's dependence on government-linked infrastructure payments, which were delayed in H1 FY26.
Treasury income is exposed to bond yield mark-to-market movements (Q4 FY26 treasury income was INR0.19 crore against INR5.6 crore a year earlier).

543259|2026-06.headline: Home First Q1 FY27: AUM up 25.7% YoY to INR16,938 crore and PAT up 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, with stable asset quality.
543259|2026-06.overview: Home First delivered strong Q1 FY27 growth, with AUM at INR16,938 crore (up 25.7% YoY, 6.7% QoQ) and disbursements of INR1,628 crore (up 31.0% YoY). Profit after tax rose 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, driven by 38.2% growth in net interest income and NIM expanding to 6.0% from 5.9%. Asset quality was flat across 1+ DPD (4.7%), 30+ DPD (3.2%) and GS3 (1.8%), and management said Q1 collections were better than usual. CFO Nutan Patwari will step down from executive responsibilities effective August 31, 2026, and the Board is evaluating candidates for the role.

financial_highlights.change: ROA +10 bps QoQ, ROE +50 bps QoQ

segments.name: Home loans (individual housing)
segments.commentary: 83% of portfolio; management said growth in both origination and disbursements was led by home loans, with housing ticket sizes up marginally.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 13-14% of portfolio; LAP growth was lower than home loans and ticket sizes were unchanged. NPA levels are broadly in line with home loans.

guidance_outlook: Expects 25% AUM growth for FY27.
Spread ex co-lending to stay within 5% to 5.25% long-term range; book spread 5.30% and incremental spread 5.40% in Q1.
Opex to AUM guided at 2.6% to 2.7% for full year; reported Q1 figure was 2.8%.
Credit cost of 40 bps in Q1; BT out expected to hold in roughly the 5% ballpark, not yet committed to 4.5% sustaining.
PLR cut considered unlikely at present given West Asia uncertainty.
NHB drawdown (currently nil, outstanding INR354 crore) planned for Q2 FY27.
Repayment rate assumption of 16% to 17% used in planning.

demand_pricing: Disbursement growth of 31% YoY split roughly 50:50 between volume (units) and ticket size, per management.

Origination yield 13.0%; portfolio yield ex co-lending 13.1%. Management said yields are held by serving the same customer segment; marginal long-term yield compression expected and to be offset by opex.
Incremental cost of borrowing 7.6%; cost of borrowing 7.8% (down 10 bps QoQ). Loan book is fully floating except one NHB scheme fixed for 7 years.
INR25 lakh-plus ticket share rose to 18% from about 12% two to three years ago; management says spreads are not materially different across ticket sizes.

Login-to-sanction ratio about 40%; origination volume growth about 10-15%.
Repayment rate 14.3% in Q1 per analyst calculation vs about 16% last year; management said there is no change in prepayment behaviour.
Stress from Surat and Tirupur tariff-affected pockets has eased; Tamil Nadu recovering after tariff and team issues.
Long-term growth focus: Uttar Pradesh, plus Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in the next 1-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no one-off; the NHB drawdown has not been taken (INR354 crore outstanding at both March and June), with a drawdown planned for Q2. Spreads are guided to a 5% to 5.25% range; book spread is 5.30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BT out fall to 4.5%, and is this industry-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited internal branch-level processes started about 5-6 quarters ago. It expects BT out in roughly the 5% range and would not commit to 4.5% without 2-3 quarters of confirmation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year opex-to-AUM guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year guidance is 2.6% to 2.7%, with a YoY reduction of 5 to 10 bps expected. Q1 opex rose due to increments and fresh hiring.

qa_highlights.question: Why was co-lending momentum weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw hiccups from changes in co-lending process and policy; management said partner banks are aligning and numbers should stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the source of disbursement growth: volume or ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 50% of growth came from unit volume and 50% from ticket size. Origination volume grew about 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for delinquencies after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 collections were excellent, with stable or improved buckets, and expects stable numbers across quarters, though Q1 is usually a seasonal uptick period.

risks_watch: Spread durability: book spread 5.30% vs incremental 5.40% and 7.6% incremental cost of borrowing; management says no one-off, but the NHB drawdown (INR354 crore, nil taken in Q1) is planned for Q2 FY27, so the Q2 borrowing cost mix is a key check.

543259|2026-09.headline: Home First Q2 FY27 AUM rose 27% YoY to Rs 18,010 crore and PAT grew 29.1% YoY to Rs 170 crore, with Stage 3 down to 1.7%.
543259|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed continued growth: disbursements of Rs 1,705 crore (+32.2% YoY, +4.7% QoQ) and AUM up 6.3% QoQ. PAT of Rs 170 crore rose 6.5% QoQ, with ROE up 40 bps to 14.9% and cost-to-income down to 30.8% from 32.7%. Gross Stage 3 improved 10 bps QoQ to 1.7% and credit cost was 40 bps. Management reiterated a 5.0-5.2% spread commitment, a 25% AUM growth target for FY27 (Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027), and exit ROE targets of 15% (FY27) and 16% (FY28). Co-lending disbursements collapsed to Rs 1.8 crore from Rs 46 crore in Q1, which management attributed to RBI guideline implementation delays.

financial_highlights.change: Stage 3 +10 bps QoQ; DPD flat QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of borrowing / incremental borrowing cost
Net worth / book value per share

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh grew strongly YoY in H1; UP, Rajasthan, NCR and Karnataka recorded strong YoY growth. Tamil Nadu returned to growth with +12% in Q2 after being marginally down in H1.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Individual housing loans are 84% of the portfolio. LAP is kept within a 20% non-housing guardrail and is running at a slower pace; management sees about 5% headroom worth 6-7 bps of spread.

segments.name: Customer segments by property type
segments.commentary: Apartments including developer-led row houses are about 30% of AUM, self-construction about 30%, plots 1-2%, and repair and renovation about 1%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth target of about 25% for FY27, implying Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027; management flagged a possible 1-2% upside from tailwinds.
Exit ROE target of 15% for FY27 and 16% for FY28 (March 2028); management said current momentum could exceed these.

Co-lending transactions expected to pick up in Q3 FY27.
Branch additions of 10-15 in the next two quarters, taking the run-rate to 20-25 per year.
capex_capacity: Network at 181 branches and 379 touch points after adding 6 branches in Q2; about 10 branches added in FY27 so far, with 10-15 more planned over the next two quarters.
Annual branch addition run-rate of 20-25; 1-2 underperforming branches are closed each year as business as usual, including recent closures in Rajasthan.
About 4,400 active connectors.

Technology: four in-house AI tools live (Cue, ClariFi, BankLens, DocIQ); over the next 18 months plans to move to a single shared data and decision platform and extend AI into sourcing, collections and servicing.
UP growth push planned for next year, with team strengthening on track.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is good across the board; rejection rates are steady and no change in leads-to-disbursement conversion.
Average new origination ticket size is about Rs 15-16 lakh; top-up is 2-3% of disbursements.
Balance transfer outflows reduced to about 4.5% from 5-6%; management guides a 4-6% range.
Origination yield ex co-lending stable at 13%; management says yield compression in the Rs 25 lakh+ segment is insignificant.
Portfolio yield fell about 10 bps QoQ to 13%, attributed to passing lower rates to new customers earlier.
Southern markets are slower because of self-construction-led demand, which takes several quarters to convert into disbursements.
Around 30% of borrowings are linked to external benchmarks; a 25 bps repo hike translates to about 10 bps in borrowing cost over time.
Hedging cost on ECB via cross-currency swaps is about 3-3.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to drought-declared districts in MP and Gujarat, and impact on disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gujarat and MP asset quality has been consistent and better than national numbers; customers are mainly in manufacturing and services, so drought impact is not seen as significant. Individual credit calls will be taken if agriculture dependence is found.

qa_highlights.question: Will spreads improve with rising rates given history of 5.5% spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 5.0-5.2% spread; 5.5%+ was only a short post-COVID phase when borrowing costs fell sharply and was not considered sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for PLR hike and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLR hike yet since borrowing costs have not moved; will reprice once borrowing cost transmits, following RBI draft guidelines. Management expects about 20 bps of cost transmission from a 50 bps cumulative repo move over 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of insurance distribution fee draft circular?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimated ROA impact of about 35 bps; about 10 bps may be conceded back by insurers, leaving 20-25 bps to recover via more LAP, more assignments, and pricing or fee changes.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending volumes fell sharply in Q2; what is happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay due to implementing new RBI guidelines with partners; management expects a visible uptick in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost decline QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campus hiring is concentrated in Q1 and Q4, so Q2 and Q3 have fewer joiners; management reiterated 2.6% opex-to-assets for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CEO succession position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no such conversation; the CEO's term runs to July 2028 and he is available for reappointment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Tamil Nadu and other southern markets lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Southern markets are largely self-construction driven with slower staged disbursements; leadership gaps in Tamil Nadu have been filled and growth is expected to reverse over the next two quarters.

Insurance distribution fee draft circular: 20-25 bps of ROA to recover through levers that are not yet executed.
Co-lending recovery in Q3 is dependent on RBI guideline implementation with partners.
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh/Telangana growth remains sub-teens or single digit, and management expects a reversal only over the next two quarters.
Stage 3 provision coverage ECL-only at 23.6%, with ECL assumptions now recalibrated quarterly and a slight uptick noted in the quarter.

rows.why: Co-lending disbursements fell to Rs 1.8 crore in Q2 from Rs 46 crore in Q1 on RBI guideline delays; management expects a visible uptick in Q3, but the book is only Rs 593 crore (3.3% of AUM).

rows.label: Tamil Nadu and southern growth reversal
rows.why: Tamil Nadu grew 12% in Q2 after lagging in H1 and leadership gaps are filled, but Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and Tamil Nadu remain sub-teens or single digit and self-construction disbursements take several quarters to convert.

543260|2026-03.headline: Stove Kraft Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, with PAT of INR6.1 crore and EBITDA margin of 9.5%.
543260|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, driven by induction cooktops (15.5% of revenue, value up 89.4% YoY) and small appliances. Gross margin held at 38.6%, flat YoY, while EBITDA rose 33.9% to INR39.5 crore at a 9.5% margin. FY26 revenue grew 10.9% to INR1,607.4 crore and EBITDA margin was 10.3%, below the roughly 11% management says it aims to protect. Management guided to upwards of 15% revenue growth in FY27, citing small appliances, export recovery and IKEA billing from Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.4 crore in Q4 FY25 (+317.8%)

financial_highlights.metric: Small kitchen appliances share of revenue (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Up from 3.8% in Q3 (YTD basis per call); FY26 10.7%

segments.name: Induction cooktops
segments.commentary: Contributed 15.5% of Q4 revenue; value +89.4% and volume +67.3% YoY. Installed capacity about 2 million units last year, with current run-rate guided at 4-5 million units.

segments.name: Small kitchen appliances
segments.commentary: Contributed 40.2% of Q4 revenue; value +12.7% YoY versus volume +97.7%, which management attributed to a mix shift toward lower-ASP products.

segments.name: Pressure cookers / cookware
segments.commentary: Pressure cooker value grew 44% YoY in Q4; non-stick cookware grew 49% YoY on stronger exports. Management said aluminium-to-stainless steel premiumisation is lifting value.

segments.name: OEM exports
segments.commentary: Q4 share 8.7% of revenue; FY26 10.7%. Management expects exports to return to about 12% of revenue, with a U.S. tariff cut from about 50% to about 18% and customer price increases from 1 June.

segments.name: Retail (EBOs)
segments.commentary: 329 exclusive brand outlets at 31 March 2026, up 67 in FY26 (16 in Q4). Average sales per store rose to INR4.7 lakh from INR3.8 lakh; retail is about 9% of revenue. Target 500 stores by 2027, and about 25 stores added per quarter.

segments.name: IKEA (new)

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at upwards of 15%, driven by small appliances, export normalisation and IKEA.
EBITDA margin: management aims to protect about 11% and improve from there. FY26 actual was 10.3%.
Gross margin: target improvement of about 1% per year, reaching about 42% within 2-3 years.
FY27 capex guided at about INR40 crore including retail. Management said net cash outflow for FY26 capex was about INR70-75 crore.

Peak capacity with existing facilities estimated at INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue.
capex_capacity: Capex capitalised in FY26 was about INR109-111 crore on the cash flow statement, but this is funded largely by supplier credit; net cash outflow is about INR70-75 crore.
Substation for electric power and one IKEA plant remain as the only significant WIP items; the main capex cycle is complete.
Induction cooktop capacity was about 2 million units last year. Additional lines are being set up at Baddi, besides Bangalore, to reach 4-5 million units at current run-rate.
Manufacturing is 97-98% in-house. Management said the capex was designed for INR3,000 crore revenue capacity.
Retail network is expanding at about 25 stores per quarter, and the company is moving to COFO/FOFO models, with franchisee-operated stores expected to be the majority within 2 years.
demand_pricing: Management cited surging induction cooktop demand after the Iran war and geopolitical supply disruptions, and said demand is shifting from an emergency option to a daily-use appliance.
Price increases of about 10% were taken in the current quarter to pass on commodity costs; export customers agreed to increases from 1 June.
GST reduction to 5% on relevant products (mid-Q3) was cited as supporting organised-player demand.
Management said it is leader by volume in induction cooktops and pressure cookers on e-commerce, but gave no market share numbers.
Forex loss in Q4 was called a one-off impact; rupee depreciation is a margin headwind. Management said it expects to pass on commodity costs but not fully on forex.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and interest cash flows high, and why did the opex rise 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex capitalised was about INR111 crore, partly funded by supplier credit (about INR32 crore). Interest rose on supplier credit and sale-and-leaseback, while borrowing costs fell. Management said freight, warranty, business promotion and sales commission grew in line with revenue; sales commission rose about INR10 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin expected to rise above 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to protect about 11% and improve from there, with growth above 15% and any upside to margin. Q4 EBITDA margin was 9.5%, hit by one-off forex loss.

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity and capex is needed to double induction production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is about 2 million units now and run-rate is 4-5 million. Added capex is small (assembly and testing lines). FY27 capex is about INR40 crore including retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are largely channel-financed (most collected within 15 days), payables are on an invoice platform (paid in 90 days versus 45-day MSME terms), and it is confident of staying in the 24-30 day range. Aluminium and steel stock was built ahead of price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Are new stores accretive, and what is the same-store growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Average sales per store rose to INR4.7 lakh from INR3.8 lakh. Management said Q4 same-store growth was 25-30% for mature stores. Franchisee economics: INR2 lakh fixed fee plus 15-30% store margin; inventory stays on company books, funded by franchisee deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IKEA revenue ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Three product lines are awarded. Revenue begins Q1 FY27, with about INR40-50 crore before FY27 year-end and INR200-250 crore at full utilisation of all three lines.

Sustainability of the induction demand surge; the pipeline refill by peers could affect growth.
Import dependence on glass (33-40% of import content), PCBs and magnets for induction cooktops, with no domestic glass capacity.

CFO transition: Subhadeep Pal takes over as CFO from 16 May 2026.

543280|2026-09.headline: Nazara Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 803 crore (up 53% YoY) and EBITDA rose 93% to INR 120 crore, helped by Bluetile and BestPlay consolidation from 1 August 2026.
543280|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter including Bluetile and BestPlay, consolidated from 1 August 2026, and Nazara reported record revenue of INR 803 crore with EBITDA margin up 311 bps to 14.9%. Gaming is now 82% of revenue and effectively all EBITDA before corporate costs. Organic gaming growth was modest at 11% revenue and 17% EBITDA, with the acquired mobile businesses doing most of the lifting. Management, under a new CEO, CFO and Executive Director, framed the next year around platform centres of excellence, AI adoption and gaming focus, and declined to give numerical growth targets. Non-core assets (NODWIN, AdTech, Absolute Sports and others) are to be monetised opportunistically.

segments.commentary: WildWorks revenue up 41% and EBITDA up 39% on Animal Jam content. Kiddopia revenue up 21% with subscribers at 5% and ARPU at $7.94 (up 8%), but EBITDA fell on higher user acquisition. Fusebox revenue down 4% on lower organic installs while EBITDA rose 7%.

segments.name: PC and console (Curve)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 77 crore (up 27%) and EBITDA INR 30 crore (up 61%), margin 38.9% versus 30.8%. Drivers were Sovereign Tower, the mobile debut of Wobbly Life and Human: Fall Flat, which has passed 60 million players.

segments.name: AdTech (Datawrkz, Space & Time)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 124 crore and EBITDA INR 0.8 crore. Management expects a temporary H2 dip as an anchor client restructures and pauses ad spend.

segments.commentary: Absolute Sports revenue INR 23 crore with adjusted EBITDA INR 1.7 crore. Pro Football Network revenue up 20% with EBITDA margin of 17% (versus -18%). Sportskeeda operating costs down 13% QoQ, with syndication revenue partly offsetting lower ad rates.

segments.commentary: Not reported in the update. H1 revenue and EBITDA are roughly flat; two IPs (I-Popstar and All That Matters) slipped from Q2 to Q3. The Rs 23 crore share of loss in Q2 reflects an EBITDA loss plus an impairment on the Turkish investee Publishme. Pre-IPO round and IPO are being prepared.

543287|2026-03.headline: Lodha FY26 presales INR205bn (+16%) and PAT INR34.3bn (20% margin); FY27 presales guided to INR240bn, PAT growth ~20% medium term.
543287|2026-03.overview: Lodha delivered its best-ever quarter in Q4 FY26 with presales of about INR58.9bn (+23% YoY), and full-year presales of INR205bn (+16%) with every quarter a record. PAT grew 24% to INR34.3bn, with PAT margin touching 20% for the first time, while adjusted EBITDA grew 14% and the embedded development margin held near 33%. Management shifted its primary guidance metric to PAT, guiding FY27 presales of about INR240bn (mid-teens growth) and PAT growth of about 20% CAGR to over INR85bn by FY31. Business development was strong, with 12 projects and INR600bn GDV added, and net debt fell to 0.23x equity.

qa_highlights.question: How ready is the FY27 INR218bn launch pipeline and what is the status of environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: New launches were about one-third of FY26 sales and will be slightly lower in FY27; all projects have land acquired, designs done and approvals available or in process. Management said the environmental clearance issue (Supreme Court order August 2025) is behind the market, with clearances resuming from November 2025.
