qa_highlights.question: Palava residential outlook for FY27 with road infrastructure completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects presales growth in the Extended Eastern suburbs to exceed company-level growth in FY27, with timing dependent on freeway and Thane highway openings; no number given.

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation impact and labour attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction cost up 3-5%, margin impact nominal; labour attrition 5-10% above seasonal norms, viewed as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Own data centre vs monetising land?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 of 400 acres to be used for own portfolio, rest sold; strategic decision to build long-term annuity income using land sale proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage fall in FY27 given strong FCF?
qa_highlights.answer: DevCo may become net debt zero over next few years; overall debt at end FY27 expected to be somewhat lower than FY26 despite annuity build-out.

543287|2026-06.headline: Lodha Q1 FY27 PAT more than doubled to INR 13.7 billion (26.9% margin) on land sales, while pre-sales rose only 4% to INR 46.3 billion.
543287|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 43% YoY to INR 50 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to INR 21.5 billion at a 43% margin, with PAT of INR 13.7 billion versus INR 6.8 billion a year ago. Management said the quarter was flattered by roughly half of the year's planned land sales, including data centre park land sold to Digital Edge India at about INR 420 million per acre. Residential pre-sales were deliberately weak because about one-third of normal launches were postponed to Q2 on Middle East conflict concerns. Net debt fell by INR 4.5 billion to under INR 50 billion, with net debt to equity at about 0.2x.

segments.name: Residential (DevCo)
segments.commentary: Pre-sales of INR 46.3 billion with only one Mumbai launch (about 0.4 million sq ft); sustenance sales drove the quarter. Premium and luxury made up almost 60% of sales, and mid-income (below INR 3 crore) about 50% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Land sales
segments.commentary: Data centre and other land pre-sales of about INR 12 billion, with PAT contribution of about INR 6 billion. Management guides land sales of INR 20-30 billion a year for the next several years.

segments.name: Annuity / RentCo
segments.commentary: June exit run-rate of about INR 3 billion with no data centre contribution. Target is over INR 30 billion by FY32, including about INR 20 billion-plus from data centres, INR 6 billion from retail and office, and INR 4 billion from warehousing and industrial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of about 20% growth on INR 34.3 billion, i.e. about INR 41 billion; Q1 delivered 33% of this. Management said 20% is an annual target and warned against annualising the quarter.
FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 240 billion reaffirmed, with H1 at 40-42% of the full year. Q2 pre-sales expected at INR 50 billion or more, with July off to a good start.
Embedded margin excluding land sales was in the early 30s; full-year margin guidance of 32-34% retained, with no expectation of margins in the 40s.
Medium-term PAT growth of about 20% a year, taking PAT beyond INR 85 billion by FY31; ROE expected to move toward 20% from about 16% in FY26 but may not reach it.
DevCo to be net debt-free within 2-3 years; net debt to equity to stay below the 0.5x ceiling.
Pricing to rise 5-7% across micro markets over the year, with room for a further 100-200 bps.
Dividend policy of 15-20% of PAT, then debt reduction, then buyback or special dividend.
capex_capacity: Data centre park: about 660 acres at Palava, with about 3 GW of power tie-up, 5 fibre routes and 5 transmission lines. About 130 acres of the first 370-acre phase is sold; about 150 more acres are to be sold over 3-4 years at about INR 600 million per acre (about INR 90 billion).

Plan to build about 1 GW of powered shell on about 90 acres, generating over INR 20 billion of annual rent by FY32. Leasing of the first box is targeted within FY27, with physical work on the company's own box to start in calendar 2026.
Estimated capex for the power-shell infrastructure is INR 500-700 crore over time, per the CFO-level answer on infrastructure.
Power density is 11-15 MW per acre. Management does not yet plan chips or racks and sees turnkey shell at least two years away.
demand_pricing: Middle East NRI buyers are about 4-5% of sales. Management sees the impact as moderate and expects NRI and US-based buyers to shift some money toward Indian homes.
Construction cost: if energy-linked inflation persists for a full year, management expects a 1-1.5% rise in project cost (35-75 bps project EBITDA impact). Supply chain is about 95% domestic.
Conversion rate reportedly 8% or higher from July, with a long-run aim of 10%.
Sales from new cities (Pune, Bangalore, NCR, MMR) to reach 30-45% of pre-sales in the medium term.

Palava land sale price rose to about INR 420 million per acre from about INR 210 million in calendar 2025. Management puts fair market value at about INR 650 million per acre, reachable in about 18 months.
Competition described as rational. Branded share of MMR is about 30%, which management expects to reach 40-45% by the end of the decade.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value and margin of the land sales in the quarter, and how much did they add to PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore of land pre-sales including data centre land, with revenue recognised at 85-90% of that. PAT contribution was about INR 600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the data centre rental estimate appear to fall from INR 30 billion to INR 20 billion-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change. The INR 30 billion FY32 target is unchanged, and data centres account for INR 20 billion-plus of it. Powered shell rent is a little over INR 20 million per MW a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the pre-sales guidance factor in the Middle East war, and is there upside if it ends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been contained and the guidance is maintained. It will review once the conflict ends. MMR high-value sales have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any margin outlook beyond the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Embedded margins excluding land were in the early 30s. Management said the 40s-level margin was driven by forward-loaded land sales and that the full-year guidance of early 30s stands.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed per acre for a data centre land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost is about 10-15% of the sales price, and the CFO put group infrastructure capex at INR 500-700 crore over time. Most of the sale price flows through to cash after tax.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company compete with its data centre buyers, and what is its competitive edge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company offers powered shell, which no other provider offers, and that its advantages are land, power, recycled water, ecosystem and relationships.

risks_watch: Pre-sales were up only 4% YoY; the FY27 target of INR 240 billion requires H2 weighting, with about INR 250 billion of GDV in the launch calendar.
Land sales are lumpy and drove a large share of PAT; the 20% PAT growth target is annual, so quarterly results will vary.
Middle East conflict is prolonged. Energy-linked construction cost inflation could reach 1-1.5% if it lasts a full year.
Data centre economics depend on signed leases, which are not yet in place. Power beyond the 3 GW tie-up is still under work, and the first lease is expected within FY27.
Connectivity openings (Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway, Upper Thane connector) are expected after the monsoon. Impact on Palava sales is expected from Q4 and meaningful mainly in FY28.

543287|2026-09.headline: Lodha H1 FY27 PAT rose 63% to INR 2,386 crore on revenue of INR 9,460 crore; management expects to beat FY27 profit guidance of about INR 4,000 crore.
543287|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 was reported as the strongest half in company history, with PAT of INR 2,386 crore (up 63%), revenue of INR 9,460 crore (up 30%) and pre-sales of INR 96 billion (up 7%). Q2 had no land sales, so management framed Q2 profitability as underlying development-business earnings. Net debt was about INR 52 billion (about 0.2x equity). Management said the festive season in October was strong and that the company expects to beat its 20% profit growth guidance comfortably, while flagging a 25 bp RBI repo hike in October with limited expected impact on the upper-ticket segment.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 pre-sales as share of FY27 guidance

segments.name: Development business (residential)
segments.commentary: Q2 earnings described as underlying development profitability with no land sales in the quarter. Management expects price growth of about 5-7% p.a. against cost growth of about 4% p.a., adding 100-200 bp margin each year.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Bangalore pre-sales exceeded INR 1,800 crore in Q2. Lodha Beaumont Estate (70-acre, North Bangalore) sold about INR 1,500 crore-plus in the first 3 months. FY26 sales were about INR 2,300 crore; FY27 pre-sales are expected above INR 3,000 crore with six operating projects by FY27 end.

segments.name: Data centre platform
segments.commentary: Power availability raised to 5 GW from 3 GW based on approvals; AWS, STT and Digital Edge are building on site. Next land transaction expected in Q4 at about INR 15 billion, with one land deal about every 6 months. First BTS box documents targeted this fiscal, with rental income from FY29.

segments.name: Palava / Extended Eastern suburbs
segments.commentary: Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway is clinically complete and expected to open within weeks. Management expects significant pre-sales uptick at Palava in CY27, though no specific sales guidance was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance maintained at about INR 24,000 crore, with H2 development pre-sales of INR 6,000-7,000 crore each in Q3 and Q4 plus a data centre land transaction of about INR 1,500 crore in Q4.
FY27 launch GDV for H2 is just under INR 20,000 crore; FY27 launch guidance was cut to INR 23,100 crore from INR 25,000 crore in July, per the analyst's reading of the slides.
Expects to beat 20% PAT growth guidance (which implied just over INR 4,000 crore) comfortably; no FY28 guidance given yet.
FY27 operating cash flow expected at about INR 85 billion.
DevCo targeted to become net debt-free in 2-3 years.
Data centre target of 1 GW BTS input power signed by FY30 and delivered by FY32; BTS rental of INR 20-23 billion per GW per annum reiterated.
capex_capacity: Construction spend run-rate of about INR 13-13.5 billion per quarter in H1 FY27; management expects a further pickup in H2 as monsoon slowdown eases.
Data centre campus power raised to 5 GW input (a little over 4 GW IT output) from 3 GW; company is funding substation build-out at its own cost.
BTS data centre: definitive documents and construction targeted in FY27 for the first box, with delivery to tenant in FY29.
About 3.9 million sq ft completed unsold inventory, unchanged QoQ; management attributed this to coincidence of delivery timing rather than a stock build-up.
Mumbai Metropolitan Region launch pipeline of about INR 100 billion GDV, of which South-Central Mumbai about INR 40 billion.
First Gurugram NCR project launched in the festive season (commercial office); two more residential pilot projects planned, with a third site possibly added.
demand_pricing: Q2 sales: a little under one-third came from new launches, with the rest from sustenance; H2 mix expected similar or slightly higher launch share.
YTD price growth about 4%; sales mix about 50% in the INR 1-5 crore band (average LTV high-40s to low-50s) and the balance above INR 5 crore.
NRI demand from the Gulf is about 4-5% of sales, mainly entry-level INR 1-3 crore homes; no other meaningful footfall impact from the West Asia situation.
Bangalore market: absorption of about INR 52,500 crore in H1 CY26, up 10% YoY; pricing up about 6% YoY; INR 2 crore-plus segment about 50% of demand.
Management says branded Grade A+/A developers are gaining share and pricing power, while commoditised supply sees less pricing traction.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment has been hit most by the West Asia war, and how is the luxury segment trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Only NRI sales from the Middle East (4-5% of sales, mostly INR 1-3 crore homes) were affected; Central Mumbai luxury demand described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 launch guidance cut to INR 23,100 crore while pre-sales guidance was held at INR 24,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said launches shift by a month or two routinely and that one project moved from Q4 into Q1 FY28 without changing the pre-sales outlook.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the data centre power upgrade to 5 GW?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects approvals received; the power is available from the existing transmission ecosystem, with the company funding substations. Management estimated $150 billion-plus of potential investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected size and land value of the next data centre transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: A multi-hundred-MW BTS transaction is expected; the land deal is expected at about high-INR 50s crore per acre versus INR 42 crore per acre in the last deal, against an earlier INR 65 crore fair-value estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Are BTS rental assumptions changing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 20 billion per GW per annum is seen as conservative; guidance of INR 20-23 billion per GW is unchanged for now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin driver behind improved profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Price growth of about 6% against cost growth of about 4% adds 100-200 bp of margin a year, plus supply-chain value extraction; management says this is blended profitability, including new cities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction cost impact from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy-intensive items such as tiles show inflation, but these are a small share of cost; the company carries a 10% construction cost contingency and 3% project revenue contingency.

risks_watch: Interest rates: 25 bp repo hike in October; INR 1-5 crore segment (about 50% of sales) has mortgage exposure, and entry-level Palava and Extended Eastern suburbs buyers are most sensitive.
Launch slippage: 1-2 H2 launches may move by a month or two, and H2 launch GDV is about INR 20,000 crore, so timing risk is material to the INR 24,000 crore pre-sales target.
Data centre execution: first BTS documents and construction are targeted in FY27 and delivery in FY29; the land deal is expected in Q4 and is a confidential, multi-hundred-MW transaction.
Construction disruption from Maharashtra air-quality rules and water scarcity in the next 3-4 months.
Construction cost inflation in energy-intensive materials as oil prices stay elevated.

segments.commentary: Total VAP INR2,969 million vs INR2,841 million in Q4 FY25; excluding bulk sales, VAP grew 21% YoY. Curd rupee sales were INR230 crore in Q4 and INR845.7 crore in FY26; consolidated VAP realisation was INR60.54/litre.

segments.name: Africa (Uganda and Kenya)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR151 crore (+48% YoY) with liquid milk volume up more than 60%; record quarterly EBITDA of INR18 crore. FY26 EBITDA margin about 11.3% vs 11% in FY25, and FY26 volume about 2.27 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 0.9 lakh).

rows.why: Possible shift of flavoured milk production to Chandel is under review, and VAP sales rose to INR414.7 crore (from INR352.8 crore), but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Further milk price correction of 2-2.5% in Q2 FY27
rows.why: Management has taken about 1.4% in Dodla standalone and about 4% in Africa and plans a further 2-2.5%, implying 4-5% for the year, with the price gap to cooperatives above INR10/litre in Tamil Nadu and INR6-7/litre in Karnataka supporting the move.

rows.label: Southern cooperatives expected to raise prices
rows.why: Amul and Mother Dairy have raised prices and management expects southern cooperatives to follow due to delayed farmer payments, which would narrow the price gap that limits share gains.

rows.label: Net debt-free balance sheet with INR689 crore net cash
rows.why: Net cash and investments of about INR689 crore with the INR590 crore capex programme funded from cash and accruals and no debt drawn.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 7-8% margin recovery, the 10% volume and 15% revenue guidance, and Africa/VAP growth, but cautious on near-term procurement and pass-through lag, and deferred on the Chandel capital allocation, Sids Farm rationale and ice cream capacity.

543306|2026-09.headline: Dodla Dairy Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% to INR1,196 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.4% as milk procurement costs outran price hikes.
543306|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.4% YoY to INR1,196 crore, with EBITDA of INR64.1 crore (5.4% margin) and PAT of INR36.6 crore (3.1% margin). Milk procurement cost rose to INR43.2/litre from INR37.3 a year ago, while the INR2.5/litre price hike taken late in the quarter (mostly September) only partly offset it, so the milk spread narrowed to INR18.7/litre from INR20. Africa was the standout at INR179 crore (+56%). Management guided to a return to 7.5-8% EBITDA margin for Oct-Dec quarter and H2 on current price levels, with procurement prices expected to stay flat.

segments.name: India dairy (milk and VAP)
segments.commentary: Milk procurement 21.3 lakh litres/day (+9.3% YoY); milk sales volume 14.2 lakh litres/day (+8.4%); milk sales realisation INR61.9/litre vs INR57.3 a year ago. Curd and curd-based products volume +23% YoY to 444.7 MT/day.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Revenue INR179 crore (+56% YoY), driven by a 68.5% rise in milk sales. Greenfield plant in Uganda on 70 acres; civil work started about a month before the call, with operations targeted for FY28 beginning.

segments.name: OSAM (Bihar/Jharkhand)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR82.37 crore at 1.33 lakh litres/day. EBITDA margin 1% in Q2 vs 2.6% in Q1; management is prioritising operational stabilisation over margin and expects 4-5% EBITDA from Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Orgafeed (cattle feed)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 40% YoY in Q2 FY27, but margins hit as raw material costs could not be fully passed on to farmers.

segments.name: Curd (within VAP)
segments.commentary: Realisation INR59.15/litre vs INR56.16 a year ago; EBITDA margin about 12%, gross margin about 19%. Buttermilk and lassi margins 20-23%.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to return to about 7.5-8% for Oct-Dec quarter and H2 FY27 at current price levels, assuming no further procurement inflation.
Full impact of the INR2.5/litre price hike to show in Q3 FY27; further hikes possible if cooperatives implement announced larger increases.
Management expects milk procurement prices to stay flat through Q3 and Q4 FY27 (only INR0.20-0.30 locational variation noted).
Maharashtra plant: liquid milk operations from March-April 2027; powder operations from September 2027.
Capex total: earlier INR600 crore estimate (Maharashtra INR280 crore, Africa INR60-70 crore, OSAM net acquisition) may rise 5-10% on inflation; a further feed plant decision is 3-6 months away.
India revenue for H2 FY27 guided at INR1,000-1,200 crore, versus management's earlier figure of INR1,300-1,400 crore.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR66 crore, mainly Maharashtra expansion; cash and bank balance INR659.4 crore as of September 2026.
Africa greenfield (Uganda) on 70 acres, targeting operations from FY28; Kenya focus on market penetration and own procurement network.
Feed capacity at about 6,000-7,000 tonnes installed, utilisable 8,000-9,000 tonnes; another feed plant for Maharashtra under consideration.
Maharashtra (Itkal) plant: liquid milk from March-April 2027, powder from September 2027.
H1 FY27 inventory build of INR76 crore (SMP and butter); inventory stood at INR232 crore at September 2026.
demand_pricing: Milk procurement cost INR43.2/litre in Q2 FY27 vs INR41 in Q1 and INR37.3 in Q2 FY26; management says the cost has peaked and was front-loaded into Q1-Q2 given unusually early price rises.
Procurement by state (lakh litres/day): Andhra Pradesh 4.76, Karnataka 5.1, Maharashtra 2.99, Tamil Nadu 4.25, Telangana 0.45.
Q1 to Q2 price-cost gap: realisation +INR1.99/litre vs procurement +INR2.93/litre sequentially; YoY realisation +INR3.3 vs procurement +INR4.84.
Consolidated realisation INR65.06/litre (vs INR62.53); India INR63.59 (vs INR63.07); overseas INR73.14 (vs INR60.11); HR Foods INR67.05 (vs INR63.36); consolidated VAP realisation INR66.46.
VAP mix in INR327 crore: curd and curd products INR251 crore, paneer INR21 crore, ghee and butter INR22.1 crore, ice cream INR11 crore, flavoured milk INR13 crore, sweets INR6.6 crore.
Packing material costs +41.6% YoY; overhead cost per litre up on inflation and geopolitical factors.
OSAM competition: Sudha (about 70% share, with late payments), ITC, Amul, and UP brands Gyan Dairy and Namaste India are entering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for milk procurement cost and pricing, and what margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes procurement prices stay at elevated levels with no dip. The Sept price hike flows through in full from Q3, and Dodla should return to 7.5-8% EBITDA for Oct-Dec and H2 at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 seasonal procurement inflation recur?
qa_highlights.answer: B.V.K. Reddy said Q1 and Q2 prices were already elevated, that no Q3 or Q4 hike is seen, and that rains in southern coastal areas have improved availability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Meadow India JV and what does it cover?
qa_highlights.answer: A 40:60 JV with Meadow India Holdings (UK-linked) to sell B2B dairy ingredients such as tailored skim milk powder and inclusions. Dodla invests INR1 crore for its 40% stake, and it is an exploratory venture.

qa_highlights.question: How will OSAM's low margin affect consolidated EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: OSAM revenue of INR250-300 crore at 4% EBITDA is about INR12 crore, so the drag is small (INR3-4 crore). India operations drive the margin recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Did the INR600 crore capex estimate change?
qa_highlights.answer: No material change. Capex may rise 5-10% on inflation. Maharashtra was earlier INR280 crore, Africa INR60-70 crore, and OSAM acquisition net of cash about INR600 crore in total.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the INR2.5/litre price hike holding and procurement prices staying flat through Q3-Q4; sustained cooperative hikes would be passed on with a lag.
Feed (concentrate) inflation expected as ethanol and CBG demand pulls maize; Orgafeed margins are under pressure.
OSAM stabilisation: own-procurement shift from agent model to direct farmer payment (25-30% done, target 70-80% by March); Sudha and new entrants competing.
El Nino and drought risk in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; buffalo milk supply declining year on year.
Maharashtra plant commissioning timelines (March-April 2027 liquid, September 2027 powder) and Uganda plant FY28 start.
Q2 deferred tax charge INR5.77 crore in H1 (CDDL first-time DTL, HR Food tax-rate change).

rows.why: A 40:60 JV with Meadow India Holdings for tailored SMP and inclusions needs only INR1 crore for Dodla's 40% stake, but it is exploratory with no revenue figure given.

rows.label: Africa growth momentum
rows.why: Africa revenue was a record INR179 crore (+56% YoY) on a 68.5% rise in milk sales, and the Kenya focus on own procurement is under way.

543308|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR 1,075 crore, but EBITDA pre-Ind AS fell 33.5% to INR 131 crore as new hospitals dragged margins.
543308|2026-03.overview: KIMS reported Q4 FY26 total revenue of INR 1,084 crore (+35.3% YoY, +8.1% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 216 crore (+6.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 19.9% versus 25.3% a year ago. Management attributed the margin compression to roughly INR 32 crore of EBITDA erosion from newer units (in operation under one year), while mature units held about 28.5-29% margins. PAT fell to INR 33 crore from INR 106 crore a year ago. Management is raising about INR 1,500 crore via QIP to cut net debt, which it says has peaked at INR 3,000-plus crore, and targets net debt to EBITDA of 1-2x from about 1x-3x currently.

segments.name: Mature units
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 862 crore with EBITDA about INR 250 crore, a margin of roughly 28.5-29%. For FY26, mature units generated INR 3,335 crore revenue and about INR 956 crore EBITDA, about 29.5% margin.

segments.name: Newer units (under one year old)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 224 crore with EBITDA erosion of about INR 32 crore. For FY26, these units generated INR 597 crore revenue and about INR 128 crore EBITDA erosion.

segments.name: Mahadevapura (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 49 crore and loss about INR 14 crore; management says it averages about INR 17 crore/month and targets INR 25-30 crore/month over 12 months.

segments.name: Electronic City / PES (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 17 crore with loss about INR 25 crore; commissioned in December 2025. Management expects EBITDA-positive by end of FY27.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 47 crore and loss about INR 5 crore. Management says Thane was EBITDA-neutral in March and April 2026, before adding doctors in May.

segments.name: Nashik
segments.commentary: Q4 loss about INR 1 crore. Still awaiting STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA empanelment.

guidance_outlook: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth guided at about 10-12% in FY27, below historical rates due to Kondapur and Kompally.
Newer-unit combined losses in FY27 and FY28 expected to be less than half of the roughly INR 120-128 crore FY26 drag, subject to insurance empanelments.
Use about INR 1,000 crore of QIP proceeds to retire debt; remainder for losses and capex in existing facilities.

Palakkad (300-bed, acquired; consolidated) expected at INR 6.5-7 crore revenue in May 2026 with about 5% negative EBITDA, breakeven by June-July 2026, targeting INR 12-15 crore/month revenue over time.
Bangalore ARPOB to be modelled at INR 75,000 annually; Andhra ARPOB at about INR 26,000-27,000.
Bengaluru occupancy expected at 35-40% by end of FY27 on full bed capacity.
Kondapur move to new 800-bed facility from first week of June 2026; Phase 1 of 400-500 beds; INR 50-75 crore further capex deferred to FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: New Kondapur (Hyderabad) 800-bed hospital; shift from old facility starting first week of June 2026, with a one-month transition and old facility possibly running 2-3 months more.
Phase 1 of Kondapur to open at 400-500 beds; remaining 300 beds to be commissioned as occupancy rises.

Expansions in FY26: Kompally (Hyderabad), two in Guntur, Thane and Sangli (Maharashtra), Mahadevapura and Electronic City (Bengaluru), Kollam (Kerala), and fertility centres in Hyderabad and Guntur. KIMS Cuddles mother-and-child unit opened in Nellore; cancer block opened in Ongole.

Greenfield projects planned in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu (one hospital), with continued expansion in Andhra and Telangana; these take 3-5 years to commission. Secunderabad expansion expected within 18 months.
Project funding norm: about 40% equity and 65% debt. Doctor participation typically 3-5% of equity; the model remains open.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per operating bed rose 13.7% YoY and 1.7% QoQ in Q4; average revenue per patient up 14% YoY and 3.5% QoQ.
IP volumes up 17.9% YoY and 4% QoQ; OP volumes up 30.1% YoY and 4.1% QoQ in Q4. FY26 IP volumes +15.4%, OP +25.4%.
Maharashtra Q4 occupancy at 60.5% (FY26 about 52.1%), which management calls the new base.
Hyderabad is the most competitive market; 4-5 hospitals commissioned in the last year. Management reports losing only one or two doctors, with no material attrition.
Insurance empanelment delays (new GIC common empanelment process and volume of new hospitals) are the main ramp-up constraint for new units.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise a INR 1,500 crore QIP after saying debt had peaked, and are new expansion plans firm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is near INR 3,000-plus crore and the QIP will retire debt, with cash flow then funding 3-5 year greenfield projects. Expansion plans are still being explored; 400-500 beds of small acquisitions may come in the next two quarters, all in home markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on insurance empanelment for the new hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Nashik still needs STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA. Thane has GIPSA, with Medi Assist and STAR nearly done, covering about 70% of insurance volume. Bangalore needs 3-4 more months. Confusion from the new GIC common-empanelment process caused the delays.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARPOB and occupancy run-rates for Bangalore and Andhra Pradesh for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore ARPOB of about INR 85,000 for FY26 but management says to model INR 75,000. Andhra at about INR 26,000-27,000 in Q3 and Q4. Bengaluru occupancy expected 35-40% by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kondapur capex and phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The 800-bed Kondapur facility is almost fully capex-complete, with INR 50-75 crore left for two additional floors in FY28-FY29. Phase 1 covers 400-500 beds. Transition cost is expected to be about INR 15-25 crore, based on the Sunshine move precedent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for FY27 after the QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of debt to be retired from QIP proceeds. The balance covers losses at new hospitals and capex in existing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA growth is expected for the Telangana cluster in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth of about 10-12% in FY27, below historical levels because of the Kondapur and Kompally commissioning.

risks_watch: Insurance empanelment delays at Nashik, Thane and Bangalore hospitals, which management says limit ramp-up.
Margin dilution from new units: cluster-level margins, not company-level, are the guided metric; Q4 company margin was 19.9%.
Leverage: management targets net debt/EBITDA of 1-2x; the call says the current ratio is about 1x-3x (ambiguous). The QIP is about INR 1,500 crore.
Q4 PAT of INR 33 crore and EPS decline of 37.2% in FY26, with management acknowledging ROE and ROCE have fallen.
Geopolitical and macro risk: management cited the Gulf war and a government austerity appeal.
Competition for doctors in Hyderabad; possible common-empanelment initiative by IRDAI/GIC, which management declined to comment on.
Inconsistencies in disclosures: bed-addition plan changed without a timeline; management said the update would come next quarter.

Management was evasive on forward-looking growth numbers and on the common-empanelment policy.

543308|2026-06.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.
543308|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total revenue of INR 1,196 crore (+36.1% YoY, +10.3% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 240 crore at a 20.1% margin, with PAT of INR 37 crore versus INR 85 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by IP volumes (+26.6% YoY) and OP volumes (+28.5% YoY), with the Kondapur hospital commissioned in June and Palakkad (Kerala) opened. The QIP raised INR 1,500 crore, of which INR 1,100-1,125 crore repaid debt, and a INR 600 crore promoter preferential allotment is partly pending. Management guided Telangana to 30-35% margins over time, Kerala to 20-22% in two to three years, and Bengaluru to break-even for the full year, while several new units are still ramping up.

financial_highlights.change: +20.1% YoY, +10.9% QoQ; margin vs 20.27% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA pre-Ind AS excluding other income

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,570 crore as of 30 June 2026; about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents (incl. liquid MF and deposits <12m)

segments.name: Telangana cluster (incl. Kondapur, Secunderabad)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue and EBITDA grew strongly YoY in Telangana and Andhra; Kondapur did INR 45 crore in July (first full month) against INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Telangana occupancy is about 61% on the adjusted bed base excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura reached EBITDA break-even in June and did about INR 20 crore revenue in July; Electronic City expected to break even in about one to two quarters. Management aims for zero EBITDA for the cluster for FY27. Census-bed occupancy at Mahadevapura is about 40%.

segments.name: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik, Nagpur)
segments.commentary: Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly revenue in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% EBITDA margin. Nashik reached EBITDA break-even in Q1; Nagpur did INR 30 crore revenue in July. Empanelment delays of four to five months weighed on Q1.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Kerala margins are in the single digits currently, with management expecting mid-teens in FY28 and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Palakkad opened, taking Kerala to three units; one more hospital (Thrissur) is due in three to four months.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management said AP remains strong. Q1 ARPOB growth slowed from prior quarters (Q4 FY26 about INR 27,000), which management attributed to seasonal case mix. Cancer services were added to most AP hospitals in the last two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Telangana EBITDA margin expected to return to 30-35% over time as new Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ramp up; management said 30% is achievable by FY30 without new beds, and 70% occupancy is targeted in three to four years.
Bengaluru cluster targeted at zero EBITDA for full FY27; Bengaluru ARPOB expected to settle at INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, versus about INR 90,000+ recently.
Kondapur full potential of about INR 100 crore revenue per month (about INR 1,200 crore a year) within four to five years; model margin around 30%, with 30-32% suggested for the next two years.
ARPOB growth guidance of 4-5% per year; management called 15-16% historical growth too aggressive to model.
Maintenance capex about INR 100 crore per year for three to four years; about INR 100-125 crore growth capex over the next nine months, including Rajahmundry construction (INR 60-75 crore in FY27).
Debt-equity intended to be kept around 2.5:1; surplus cash to go to greenfield and brownfield growth in core states. Minority interest about 10.5% currently, 10-15% longer term.
Empanelment with the remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, expected by end-August to mid-September 2026.
capex_capacity: Kondapur hospital commissioned in June 2026 (first patient 20 June); about 450-500 operational beds added in the last 10 days of Q1, and the old Kondapur hospital will run for about six more months with rent of about INR 90 lakh per month plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year of operating cost.

Palakkad (Kerala) opened in Q1; Thrissur to commence in three to four months; Electronic City and other Bengaluru beds added at Mahadevapura (operational beds up from about 170 to 210, total cluster 280 to 340).
Secunderabad: old 250-bed facility demolished; replacement facility expected by end of next year.

Two O&M agreements (Golden Lan Solutions, Sarvottam Healthcare) approved in draft: a 300-bed Telangana hospital near Kondapur with INR 90-95 crore monthly revenue potential, and a Kakinada hospital currently at INR 7-8 crore a month, targeting INR 15-20 crore. O&M means no losses borne by KIMS.

543311|2026-09.headline: India Pesticides Q2 FY27 revenue fell 22% YoY to INR 231 crores and PAT to INR 18 crores, while management guides to roughly flat FY26 revenue.
543311|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue declined 22% YoY to INR 231 crores, with EBITDA of INR 33 crores (14.4% margin vs 18.2%) and PAT of INR 18 crores (vs INR 32 crores). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 487 crores, down 15.9%, with export revenue at INR 177 crores vs INR 229 crores. Management cited geopolitical disruption, deficient monsoon rains, softer overseas herbicide demand and higher job-work and employee costs. Management says export orders for the coming quarter have been received and aims to make up H1 shortfall in H2, targeting revenue at least equal to FY26.

segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 111 crores, up from INR 72 crores in the prior quarter. Management said the figure includes bulk formulation exports, but formulation share still rose YoY after excluding incremental bulk sales.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 export revenue was INR 177 crores vs INR 229 crores a year earlier. New approvals in UK (insecticide, technical equivalence) and Argentina (herbicide) were received; Argentina is expected to add INR 20-25 crores in year one.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to deliver revenue at least equal to FY26 for the full year, with H2 similar to or slightly better than H2 FY26 to partly recover H1 shortfall.
Management is confident of maintaining Q2's 14.4% EBITDA margin going forward.
Export orders of about INR 100 crores from Europe and Australia were cited, partly executed and partly to be executed in coming months.

Argentina is a fresh market with no prior business; UK sales will be through existing customers under letters of access. EU sales are via formulators only.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of maintaining the Q2 EBITDA margin; raw material is more than 65% India-sourced and about 20% from China.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new export orders and can they drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are a mix of technical and bulk formulation (WDG and EC) for existing molecules, covering Europe and Australia, with about INR 100 crores in size; management expects to cover the H1 shortfall in the next six months.

qa_highlights.answer: Job-work charges rose to about INR 12 crores from INR 6 crores as an intermediate moved to job work; formulation growth partly reflected bulk exports but formulation share rose YoY.

543318|2026-03.headline: Clean Science Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR193 crore with 46% EBITDA margin; FY26 standalone revenue fell 12% to about INR796 crore.
543318|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to about INR193 crore on volume recovery, with EBITDA of INR88 crore (46% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (40%), but revenue fell 19% YoY. For FY26, standalone revenue declined 12% from INR900 crore to INR796 crore, attributed to loss of an FMCG key account (4-MAP), lower offtake and pricing pressure. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 72% of FY26 standalone revenue. Management cited a rebound in flagship product volumes and a gross margin (RMC 33%) about 2 points better than prior quarters.

segments.name: Pharma-Agro (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of FY26 standalone revenue. The pharma intermediate plant was refurbished for HALS intermediates, and the older pharma intermediate was dropped.

segments.name: FMCG (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed the balance 9% of FY26 standalone revenue. A key FMCG account (4-MAP) was lost during the year.

segments.name: HALS (Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4 FY26, at over 1,000 tonnes per quarter versus about 350-360 tonnes eight quarters earlier. Blended realisation was about INR460/kg versus INR420-430/kg in Q3; exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%. Subsidiary EBITDA margin was about 15% in Q4 versus about 1% in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Performance Chemical 2 (water treatment-related capex) expected to commercialise by September 2026; validation in Q3, initial commercial production in Q4, and a pickup in FY28.
Hydroquinone/Catechol plant expected to reach optimal operations in 1-2 quarters; captive HQ/catechol now replaces imports for TBHQ and Veratrole.
Capex budget for FY27 of about INR80-100 crore; Clean Fino-Chem projects under an INR200 crore enabling Board resolution, with investment likely in the second half of FY27.
Management aspires to a HALS blended realisation of USD7-7.5/kg but did not give FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, calling FY27 a 'very tricky' year dependent on macro and crude oil.
Management said it is not pencilling in any price hikes; it expects to benefit in an inflationary environment, as it did in FY23.
capex_capacity: Clean Fino-Chem Hydroquinone/Catechol plant commissioned in December 2025; still in initial stabilisation, with utilisation about 10-15% and March 2026 HALS exit utilisation about 40%.
Performance Chemical 2 commercialisation timeline moved due to scarce manpower linked to labour movement from higher gas prices; now targeted by September 2026.
Plans to debottleneck HALS lines and add a dedicated HALS 2020 line (in-house technology, validated with European customers) and to backward-integrate further key intermediates with minimal capex.
Pharma plant refurbished in the next couple of months to produce HALS intermediates, replacing Chinese sourcing.
Subsidiary capital infusion of about INR200 crore in FY26 takes total investment in subsidiary to INR750 crore.
demand_pricing: MEHQ: management is maintaining market share by calibrating prices against Chinese hydroquinone producers, who are less affected by raw material costs. Phenol and acetone prices rose sharply, and long-term contracts (half-yearly or yearly) could not pass on increases; these will be renegotiated on expiry.

HALS demand: export share rose to about 50% in select products (Europe, Middle East, US), with Southeast Asia and LatAm being explored. Distribution partners are adding safety stock, and inbound customer interest is rising.
Anisole: management said it is the largest producer and consumer globally and India; competition from China does not affect its sales, as anisole is mainly used captively.
Base chemical prices reportedly rose about 2x in some commodities, but management said these are not transactional benchmarks. Management said China has a pricing advantage over other geographies.
Management declined to share product-wise revenue, geographic split, or product-level volumes, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HALS revenue jump sharply, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer validation and trials delayed the response by several quarters. Exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%, with over 1,000 tonnes sold in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company passing on higher raw material costs (phenol, acetone, ammonia)?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were passed on partly, not fully; long-term contracts could not be repriced, and these are to be renegotiated as they expire. Q4 subsidiary EBITDA was INR8 crore despite March price spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Performance Chemical 1 (HQ/catechol) utilisation and breakeven outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 10-15%. Management expects two more quarters to optimise norms and yields before ramping utilisation further.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a volume or gross margin explanation for MEHQ, given the share-defence pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sequential growth of 7-8% was volume-led, led by flagship products. Standalone gross margin improved on product mix, with no one-off gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and the performance bonus reversal amount?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex could be INR80-100 crore, with Clean Fino-Chem investments likely in the second half. The bonus reversal was about INR11 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material and commodity volatility (phenol, acetone, ammonia, crude) and the lag in passing on costs under long-term contracts.
Pricing competition in MEHQ from Chinese hydroquinone producers and possible new capacity from Vinati Organics and Gem Aromatics in anisole, MEHQ and BHA.
HQ/catechol plant ramp-up and yield norms; utilisation at about 10-15% still needs to improve.
Performance Chemical 2 commissioning slipping further due to manpower constraints.
Standalone revenue down 12% in FY26 after loss of a key FMCG account; sustained volume recovery needs to be confirmed in Q1 FY27.
543318|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on HALS momentum and margins, but cautious on the macro outlook and FY27, with no numerical guidance. Management was evasive on product-level data, competitor details and volume targets, citing competitive sensitivity.
key_quotes: We continue to see scale in our HALS business segment, which saw the highest ever revenue in Q4 FY26 with continued improvement in favorable product mix.
This is going to be a very tricky financial year for chemical industry in my view.
Today, we stand at 50% export in select products. So our exports have picked up dramatically.
